Caltrans was unable to provide complete snow reports for the stormy conditions around the Holiday as provided a partial report for the 23rd to 25th of 78 inches at their Kingvale station. This was due to the immense workload caused by the series of winter storms that lead to many miles of blocked roadways due to snow, downed trees and powerlines as well as reduced visibility. Traffic was closed to through traffic on I-80 for several days as crews worked to clear snow and debris. The closure was approximately from 11:00am on December 25th through 8:30 am on December 29th. Chain controls continued into 10:30am on December 30th on I-80. When I-80 finally opened after being closed for several days, only essential travel was allowed. Most mountain roads were impacted in the Sierra with closures of HWY 50, 89, and 20. Many back roads were also reported to be impassible due to the winter conditions.

Temperatures dropped below the critical threshold of 28 degrees for several days in late February. Several locations in the region reported temperatures as low as 25 degrees during the event with subfreezing conditions persisting for several hours each day. The Colusa County agricultural commissioner reported that severe crop damage was likely across much of Zone 16 in the Sacramento Valley. They also mentioned the disaster threshold is 30% damage across the entire county, and the damage from this event may have spanned as many as five counties in the region. Zone 16 region was reported to have seen the most extensive damage from the cold snap with one farmer in Sutter county reporting as much as 60% of his orchard was damaged. Farmers anticipate total damage to their orchards to be determined when crops are harvested.

Onn the 25th, the Redding airport reported a low of 25 degrees and the Red Bluff airport reported a low of 28 degrees both setting new records for that day. For the month of March, the U.S. Drought Monitor degraded approximately the western half of the zone to extreme drought and kept the remainder of Zone 14 in severe drought. The zone saw emerging drought impacts due to the below average precipitation and relatively dry conditions the first few months of the calendar year. These impacts are similar to the previous year. However, reported impacts are more pronounced this March.

For the month of March, the U.S. Drought Monitor degraded all of Zone 15 to extreme drought. The zone saw emerging drought impacts due to the below average precipitation and relatively dry conditions the first few months of the calendar year. These impacts are similar to the previous year. However, reported impacts are more pronounced this March. Impacts to the region include; little to no allocation of water from irrigation districts to agriculture, reduced rangeland forage by as much as 85% without alternative forage, hay prices at record levels due to hay production elimination, cattle being sold, including calves that are typically sold in late Fall, as well as increasing reports of dry wells. The local economy has been significantly impacted.

However, reported impacts are more pronounced this March. Impacts to the region include; little to no allocation of water from irrigation districts to agriculture, hauling of water, reduced rangeland forage by as much as 85% without alternative forage, hay prices at record levels due to hay production elimination, livestock stress, cattle being sold, including calves that are typically sold in late Fall, early weaning and shipping of cattle to summer range, as well as increasing reports of dry wells. The local economy has been significantly impacted.

For the month of March, the U.S. Drought Monitor degraded the far northern border of Yolo County in zone 17 to extreme drought and kept the majority of the zone in severe drought. The zone saw emerging drought impacts due to the below average precipitation and relatively dry conditions the first few months of the calendar year. These impacts are similar to the previous year. However, reported impacts are more pronounced this March. Some of the impacts the region saw included; reduced forage, decreased stock weights, livestock stress, selling of livestock, decrease in water allocation including zero planned water deliveries from the Yolo County irrigation district, increased reports of dry wells including domestic wells, hauling of water, and plans to fallow large areas of cropland.

Some of the impacts the region saw included; reduced forage, decreased stock weights, livestock stress, selling of livestock, decrease in water allocation, increased reports of dry wells including domestic wells, hauling of water, and plans to fallow large areas of cropland.

For the month of March, the U.S. Drought Monitor degraded the far southeastern borders of the zone in Stanislaus and Tuolumne Counties. The remainder of the zone was kept in severe drought. The zone saw emerging drought impacts due to the below average precipitation and relatively dry conditions the first few months of the calendar year. These impacts are similar to the previous year. However, reported impacts are more pronounced this March including reductions to planned irrigation for agriculture.

Lake Shasta Dam saw high temperatures reach 100 to 111 degrees during the event. The hottest days were on the 6th when the high was 110 and 111 on the 7th; these were both daily records. Morning lows were also high, dropping only to 78 on the 8th and 80 on the 9th. The minimum of 80 was the highest ever in September, breaking the record of 79 set on the 10th in 2011.
The Burney Basin region saw high temperatures reach 97 to 105 degrees during the event. The hottest day was the 6th, with a high of 105 at Soldier Mountain.

The Central Sacramento Valley region saw high temperatures reach up to 115 degrees during the event. Low temperatures were in the low to upper 70s. The hottest day was on the 6th, with Marysville recording a high temperature of 115 and a low of 73, Oroville Municipal Airport 111 and a low of 75, Beale AFB 110 and low of 72, and at Chico Municipal Airport 111 and low of 75. Oroville COOP reported 113 on the 6th, with a low of 72,  with a high of 111 and a low of 79 on the 7th.

The Southern Sacramento Valley region saw all-time, monthly and daily record highs set, reaching up to 116 degrees during the event. On the 6th Downtown Sacramento recorded a high temperature of 116, which broke the all-time record high of 114 degrees set on July 17, 1925. This also broke the September record of 113 which was set the day before on the 5th. The previous monthly record of 109 was set on September 1, 1950, and tied on September 2, 1955 and September 6, 2020. The record of consecutive days over 110 was tied at 2. Daily highs were also set with 113 on the 5th and 8th and 109 on the 7th. The low of 80 on the 7th was the warmest on record in September and in all months was surpassed only on July 23, 2006, which had a low of 84. Sacramento International Airport set an all-time daily record high of 116 on the 5th and 6th, and also set a record of 4 consecutive days of 110 or higher. Sacramento Executive Airport set an all-time daily record high of 114 on the 5th and 6th. The Sacramento County Coroner attributed the death of one unhoused 49 year old man to the heat, having died while in a hospital.

The Delta regions saw high temperatures reach up to 116 degrees. Fairfield/Travis AFB reached 116 on the 5th and 6th, while the COOP station in Fairfield recorded 114 on each date. Highs remained above 100 from the 1st to the 10th. The highest low was 75 on the 7th at Fairfield COOP, and 76 at Fairfield/Travis AFB on the 6th.

The Northern San Joaquin Valley saw high temperatures reach 102 to 115 degrees during the heat event, with all-time, monthly, and daily record highs set. The all-time record high of 115 for Stockton Airport was tied on the 6th, previously set on July 23, 2006. The monthly record high was broken, which was 114 on July 14, 1972. Daily records were also set on the 5th and 8th with highs of 112 and tied on the 4th with a high of 105, and 106 on the 9th. Stockton saw a mild low of only 79 on the 8th. Modesto Airport had a September record high of 112 set on the 6th, with daily record highs of 107 set on the 5th and 108 on the 8th, with a record-tying high of 107 on the 7th. Modesto saw a mild low of only 79 on the 8th.

events.cz_name: MOUNTAINS SOUTHWESTERN SHASTA COUNTY TO WESTERN COLUSA COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The western foothills of the Sacramento Valley saw high temperatures reach upwards of 100 to 114 degrees during the event, with very warm lows in the 80s. The hottest days were the 5th and 6th when Stonyford reached 114 and Eagle Peak reached 102 each day. On the 6th Eagle Peak had a low of only 88. Arbuckle Basin reached 102 on the 5th and 104 on the 6th, with a low of only 89 on the 6th.

The northeastern foothills of the Sacramento Valley saw high temperatures reach upwards of 106 to 112 degrees during the heat event, with very warm lows in the upper 70s to 90. The hottest days were the 5th and 6th. Cohasset had a high of 110 with a low of 86 on the 5th, a high of 112, and a low of 90 on the 6th.  Jarbo Gap had a high of 106 and a low of 77 on the 5th and a high of 109 and a low of 81 on the 6th.

The Motherlode region saw high temperatures reach upwards of 109 to 115 degrees during the heat event, with lows in the upper 70s to mid-80s. The hottest days were the 5th and 6th: Auburn Airport high of 109 and a low of 77, then a high of 111 and a low of 82, Placerville Airport high of 104 and a low of 82, then a high of 108 and a low of 82, Reader Ranch high 113 and a low of 74 then a high 115 and a low of 76, and Nevada County Air Park in Grass Valley a high 104 and a low of 81 and then a high 108 and a low of 81.

Portions of Western Plumas County and Lassen National Park saw high temperatures reach up to 97 to 108 degrees during the heat event, with ranging from the mid-60s to around 80.  The hottest days were the 5th and 6th: Quincy Road had highs of 107 and 108, Chester 101 each day, Lassen Lodge 105 and 104, and Cashman 103 each day.

Portions of the West Slope of the Northern Sierra saw high temperatures reach up to 95 to 107, with lows in the 70s to around 80.  The hottest days were the 5th and 6th. Blue Canyon had a high of 95 with a low of 78 on the 5th, a high of 96, and a low of 78 on the 6th. The previous monthly record high was 93 set on September 5, 2020, and the previous monthly record maximum low was 77 set on September 6, 2020. Other notable area high temperatures on the 5th and 6th: 103 and 105 at Bald Mountain, 105 and 107 at Beaver, 103 and 104 at White Cloud, and 103 and 105 at Elizabeth. Even Duncan RAWS at an elevation of 7,182 feet reached 90 and 89.

The Northern Sacramento Valley saw daily records broken, with high temperatures reaching 110 to 115 degrees, and with low temperatures reaching up to 90. Redding Airport reached 115 degrees on the 6th (old record 111 in 2020), with Red Bluff peaking at 114 (old record 113 in 2020). On the 8th Redding Airport reached 112 degrees (old record 109 in 1923), with Red Bluff peaking at 113 (old record 112 in 1944). On the 9th Redding Airport reached 112 degrees (old record 110 in 1944), with Red Bluff peaking at 112 (tying the old record of 112 in 1944). On the 9th Redding recorded a daily record high minimum temperature of 87 degrees and Red Bluff 82 degrees.

The Dutch Fire started on September 13th at 1 pm PDT on I-80WB, near the Dutch Flat off-ramp. Winds were generally light over the area, around 5-10 mph with gusts less than 20 mph. Humidity hovered in the 20-30% range with temperatures in the upper 70s.|Around 1:30 pm PDT lane and ramp closures of I-80 began, along with evacuations of nearby residents. At 2 pm PDT I-80WB was closed and by 3:15 PM PDT it was closed in both directions. At 3:10 pm PDT a power outage was reported along I-80 from Applegate to Colfax, impacting 1785 customers. Around 5:30 pm PDT reports of progress stopped and evacuations were lifted, with 26 acres burned.

The Mosquito Fire started on September 6th, which had all-time record high temperatures in the area set and extremely low humidity dropping into the single digits. Extreme fire behavior was observed due to the very dry humidity and fuels, with the fire developing large plumes that radar indicated extended up to 40,000 feet. In the first few days, the fire saw rapid growth at 5,705 acres by 7 pm PDT on the 7th and 13,705 acres by 8 pm PDT on the 8th. More than 11,000 people were evacuated and 9,000 structures were threatened. The fire included areas in both the Tahoe and Eldorado National Forests. The fire burned a total of 76,788 acres and caused road closures throughout the area. There were 2 firefighters injured during the fire. A total of 78 structures were destroyed and an additional 13 buildings were damaged in the towns of Foresthill, Volcanoville, and Michigan Bar. Periods of moderate to heavy rain from September 18-21 largely halted fire growth, but the fire was not considered fully contained until October 22.

CalTrans reported a storm total of 16 inches of snow at Castle Peak and 15 inches at Kingvale. Central Sierra Snow Lab reported 17 inches for the entire event, while a CDEC SNOTEL reported 8 inches at Blue Canyon. Eastbound I-80 was closed on November 1 from 4 pm until 6:35 pm to all traffic and I-80 was closed to big rigs in both directions with chain controls in effect for Sierra highways. I-80 was closed again around 7 am November 2 after an accident near the summit. I-80 eastbound remained closed until 11:05 am November 2 from Cisco Grove east. US 50 was closed from 5:15 pm to 6 pm on November 1, and again on the morning of November 2. Closure info is courtesy of CalTrans District 3.

There was a male fatality due to drowning in a submerged car, confirmed by Cosumnes Fire Department near SR 99 and Dillard Rd. A levee breech on the Cosumnes River caused the flash flood. This was one of three drowning deaths reported from the flash flood event. The Cosumnes Fire Department said they rescued dozens of people in the area over the past 24 hours. A helicopter from Metro Fire also rescued several people in the area. SR 99 remained closed due to flooding on the roadway. Several vehicles are still stuck in the flood waters. Wilton firefighters responded to 25 vehicles stranded in flood water and half a dozen fallen power lines. They also cleared many downed trees from the roadways as they navigated around Wilton.

Sacramento County Sheriff confirmed a drowning on January 4 associated with the December 31 - January 1 flash flood event. A female body was found inside a vehicle. This was the third drowning associated with the event. This flooding was due to levee breaks on the Cosumnes River.

The California Highway Patrol on January 4 reported a fatality associated with the December 31 - January 1 flash flood due to levee breaks. A female body was found outside a vehicle near Dillard Road east of CA-99. This is one of three confirmed fatalities from this event.

The Cosumnes River rose rapidly due to very heavy rains and already elevated levels from previous storms. Sacramento County OES confirmed the levee along the Cosumnes River breached in three locations overnight, causing flash flooding in the surrounding areas from Rancho Murieta to Wilton. SR 99 between Dillard Rd and Grantline Rd was flooded with numerous vehicles stuck in flood waters, requiring water rescues and was closed around midnight due to flooding. Flooding continued well into January. Sacramento County issued an evacuation warning overnight for the Wilton area, changed to a shelter-in-place warning a couple of hours later due to unsafe travel conditions with surrounding flooded areas. There were an estimated 3,200 to 3,500 people in the impacted area. There were three drownings attributed to the flooding, each entered as an individual event.

Boreal Ski Resort measured 40 inches of new snow, Central Sierra Snow Lab measured 29.9 inches, Dodge Ridge Ski Resort measured 22, Kirkwood 34 inches, Sierra at Tahoe 36 inches, Sugar Bowl 34 inches. Winds in the mountains gust to 45 to 65 mph. Snow with the strong gusty winds brought whiteout conditions at times with extended closures at the Sierra passes. Tree down across Schell Rd. There was a gust to 42 mph measured at Modesto Airport.
Tree down across Italian Bar Rd. There was a gust of 37 mph measured at nearby Columbia Airport.
Tree down across Mountain Ranch Rd. There was a gust of 65 mph measured at the Airola Road PGE station.
There was a large tree reported down across SR12. There was a gust to 38 mph measured at Mills Ave in eastern San Andreas.
Tree down across the westbound lane of SR88. There was a gust of 45 mph measured at Mount Zion RAWS.
Tree and powerlines across the entire roadway of SR26. There was a gust of 40 mph measured at Barton PGE.
There were 2 trees reported down into powerlines by the California Highway Patrol. Winds gusted to 41 mph at Westover Field - Amador County Airport.
California Highway Patrol reported a tree down on Latrobe Rd. There was a gust to 50 mph reported at the Bass Lake Road - El Dorado PGE gauge.
There was a tree reported down blocking the roadway with communications lines down.
Trees and powerlines were down blocking SR193.
There was a gust of 65 mph measured at 2ENE Carson Hill.
There was a gust of 59 mph measured at 6NNW Hodson.
A large horse barn was picked up and moved over/across a 5-foot fence from winds from a severe thunderstorm straight line winds. Based on radar and damage photos, winds were around 75 mph.

A brief EF-1 tornado touched down near a small reservoir and Hogan Dam Road and continued NE for approximately 0.4 miles. It caused extensive tree damage to white oak and pine trees with trees uprooted and topped. The approximate path length was 0.4 miles with a path width of 50 yards and max winds of 90 mph.
Thunderstorm wind caused damage to metal roofing and siding on a hay barn, with the time estimated from radar.
Wires were down from a fallen tree and northbound lanes of Central Ave were blocked. Gusts to 41 mph were reported at McClellan Airfield.

A woman was reported to have died after a tree fell on her while she was in a tent near the 700th block of North 5th Street, near downtown Sacramento. Sacramento Fire Department PIO reported the tree fell due to strong winds. Gusts to 30 to 40 mph were measured in the area.
A transformer was reported by the California Highway Patrol to be sparking and causing a small fire in a tree. Wind gusts to 41 mph were reported at McClellan Airfield.

The California Highway Patrol reported a tree down in the road, in eastbound lanes and partially westbound lanes of Virginiatown Rd near Lost River Rd. Wind gusts to 48 mph were reported at Lincoln Airport.
The California Highway Patrol reported a tree down in the road, Gladding Rd near Fleming Rd. Wind gusts to 48 mph were reported at Lincoln Airport.
A trained spotter in Grass Valley measured a 71 mph gust with an anemometer. There was a tree down and minor damage near his home.

There were high winds around midnight for the Sacramento metro area, bringing numerous reports of damage. There were widespread downed trees, power lines, and power outages. McClellan Airfield measured a 68 mph gust with an anemometer at 11:35 AM. Sacramento International Airport measured a 63 mph gust with an anemometer at 00:15 AM and a 73 mph gust at 00:53 AM. Sacramento Executive Airport measured a 63 mph gust with an anemometer at 00:15 AM.
A man was reported to have died after a tree fell on him while he was in a tent near Tri Stations Road in North Highlands.  Winds were gusting to 38 to 54 mph at nearby McClellan Airfield.

Heavy snow fell, with Lower Lassen Peak receiving 30 inches of storm total snowfall between the 7th and the 11th. The National Operational Hydrologic Remote Sensing Center estimated 1 to 4 feet of storm total snow over the Lassen Area and western Plumas County. The heavy snow with gusty winds caused mountain road closures across the area.

Sacramento County completed a preliminary estimate of a total of $133 million from public storm damage from January 1 through January 17, and a total of almost $700,000 in private property damage. There was extensive levee damage and flooding along the Cosumnes River from Rancho Murieta to Wilton. There was also widespread flooding of streams, creeks, and roadways across the county. Large numbers of trees were reported down from strong wind events, with widespread power outages and reports of damage to homes and cars.

Colusa County completed a preliminary estimate of damage to roads, road closures, debris removal, and high river levels of about $800,000 in damage. The Colusa Boat Landing had some damages to the private levee, with an estimate of about $200,000.

Heavy snow with accumulations of 1-2.5+ inches per hour from a strong winter storm resulted in the closure of both East and West bound lanes of Interstate 80 from Colfax to the Nevada State line around 11 AM PST on January 10th. Blue Canyon Airport ASOS reported visibility of less than 1/4 mile in heavy snow. The area also saw wind gusts up to 40-50 mph, bringing whiteout conditions. US Highway 50 at Echo Summit was also closed for avalanche control. Caltrans also reported closures of other mountain highways due to heavy snow. |Caltrans and area ski resorts reported multiple feet of snow from January 7-12, 2023. UC Berkeley Central Sierra Snow Lab reported 56.6 inches, Bear Valley resort reported 64 inches, Boreal Ski Resort reported 46 inches, Dodge Ridge Ski Resort reported 60 inches, Kirkwood Ski Resort reported 50 inches, Sierra-at-Tahoe Ski Resort reported 45 inches, Soda Springs Ski Resort reported 46 inches, Sugar Bowl Ski Resort reported 56 inches, and Caltrans reported 48 inches at Kingvale for storm total snowfall.

There were high winds around midnight with significant damage to the Sacramento Yacht Club. Sacramento International Airport measured a 63 mph gust with an anemometer at 00:15 AM and a 73 mph gust at 00:53 AM. Sacramento Executive Airport measured a 63 mph gust with an anemometer at 00:15 AM.

There were high winds around midnight with many trees down at the Sacramento Zoo, but no animals or staff were injured. The zoo was closed through Tuesday January 10 for cleanup. Sacramento International Airport measured a 63 mph gust with an anemometer at 00:15 AM and a 73 mph gust at 00:53 AM. Sacramento Executive Airport measured a 63 mph gust with an anemometer at 00:15 AM.

Glenn County completed a preliminary estimate of damage from flooding. There was substantial flooding, resulting in the closure of more than 25 roads. There was over $5 million in damage to public infrastructure. There was significant bank erosion on a number of major creeks, stream, and the Sacramento River.

San Joaquin County completed a preliminary estimate of damage from flooding. There was substantial flooding, with around $24.7million in individual assistance/private property loss including 172 properties destroyed and 194 properties with major damage. There was around $82 million in public damages. The estimated grand total as of January 26 was $106.9 million.

Tehama County completed a preliminary estimate of damage from flooding. There was substantial flooding, with a rough estimate of $14 million in damages, mainly from 3 bridges, 1 completely destroyed by under cutting, two others under cut and sink holes, but still standing. Kirkwood Bridge $6,110,000.00 , Rawson Bridge $4,000,000.00. Remainder in trees, bridge clearing, road damage, labor $4,000,000.00||The city of Red Bluff estimated $60,000.00 bridge, trees, sandbags, labor (still climbing as they find more). The city of Corning estimated $100,000.00 road damage, creek and bridge clearing and labor. The city of Tehama estimated $27,000.00 road damage to East Gyle, tree clean up and debris clean up from roads.
Yolo County completed a preliminary estimate of damage from flooding, which is around $11 million in damages for the county and its partners.

Caltrans reported storm total snow amounts of 68 inches at Kingvale and 83 inches at Soda Springs. Ski resorts reported 67 inches at Kirkwood Mountain Resort, 63 inches at Sierra-at-Tahoe, 92 inches at Palisades Tahoe, and 62 inches at Sugar Bowl Resort. UC Berkeley Central Sierra Snow Lab reported 87.2 inches storm total. California Highway Patrol reported the closure of mountain highways due to heavy snow and strong wind, including Highway 50 and Interstate 80. Local weather stations reported strong winds, with gusts to 52 mph on Cole Creek Road (PGE 5854 feet), 41 mph on Spring Valley Road (PGE 3946 feet), 57 mph on Donner Pass Road (PGE 7636 feet). Local broadcast media reported the closure of numerous schools in the Sierra, with extensive power outages.

Caltrans reported traffic was held off and on through the late afternoon and evening of the 5th due to spin-outs. Ski resorts reported more than a foot of snow through February 4-6, 2023. For storm total snowfall UC Berkeley Central Sierra Snow Lab reported 20.9 inches, Kirkwood Ski Resort reported 17 inches, Sierra-at-Tahoe Ski Resort reported 15 inches, Sugar Bowl Ski Resort reported 21 inches, and 18 inches at Palisades Tahoe. Caltrans reported 11 inches at Kingvale, 11 inches at Eagle Lakes, and 8 inches of Blue Canyon.

Trained spotters in Quincy, CA reported storm total snow amounts of 16 to 22 inches. Lower Lassen Peak weather station reported 21.8 inches of storm total snow. Shingletown Cocorahs reported 20 inches of storm total snow, and Chester Cocorahs reported 30 inches of snow. Gusty winds were observed with this storm, with 47 mph reported at Humbug Summit RAWS, 45 mph reported at Colby Mountain RAWS, and 48 mph reported at Hatchet Mountain. Widespread power outages were reported.
The National Operational Hydrologic Remote Sensing Center estimated 10 to 20 inches fell for storm total snow.

A trained spotter at SIMS reported 22 inches at an elevation of 2800 feet. The National Operational Hydrologic Remote Sensing Center estimated 6 to 24 inches fell for storm total snow. Interstate 5 northbound was closed at Fawndale due to winter weather conditions.

events.cz_name: MOUNTAINS SOUTHWESTERN SHASTA COUNTY TO WESTERN COLUSA COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The National Operational Hydrologic Remote Sensing Center estimated 8 to 24 inches for storm total snow.
The National Operational Hydrologic Remote Sensing Center estimated 4 to 18 inches of storm total snow. Widespread power outages and school closures were reported.

CoCoRaHS reported heavy storm total snow amounts, with 29.4 inches near Nevada City, 15.6 inches near Volcano, 10.4 inches near Camino, 26.3 inches near Grass Valley, and5 inches in Placerville. An 80 year old woman was killed when the porch of a house collapsed in Foresthill under the weight of snow, with about 4 feet of snow reported on the ground by Foresthill spotter. Widespread power outages were reported with multiple schools closed. Broadcast media reported the roof collapse of a church in Foresthill due to snow load, with no injuries reported.

Lower Lassen Peak weather station reported 10 inches of storm total snow. Shingletown 5.4 ENE CoCoRaHS reported 0.2 inches of snow, and Chester Cocorahs reported 1 inch of snow. Gusty winds were observed with this storm, with 70 mph reported at 2.2 NW Pulga (PG&E), 46 mph reported at Carpenter Ridge RAWS, and 58 mph reported at Camel Peak (PG&E).

Caltrans reported a storm total snow amount of 42 inches at Soda Springs. Ski resorts reported 47 inches at Kirkwood Mountain Resort, 39 inches at Sierra-at-Tahoe, 53 inches at Palisades Tahoe, and 45 inches at Sugar Bowl Resort. UC Berkeley Central Sierra Snow Lab reported 57.1 inches storm total. California Highway Patrol reported the closure of mountain highways due to heavy snow and strong wind, including Highway 50 and Interstate 80. Interstate 80 was closed in both directions from Colfax to CA/NV stateline from 1:30 PM 2/23 to 10:40 AM 2/24. Traffic was held on US Highway 50 eastbound to South Lake Tahoe for around 4 hours on 2/23. Several other highways across the mountains were also closed. Local media reported area schools were closed. Local weather stations reported strong winds, with gusts to 59 mph at Duncan RAWS, 54 mph at Tahoe Donner RAWS (along I-80), and 45 mph at Alpha DRI.

Heavy snow and wind brought dangerous driving conditions with area road closures. Trained spotters in Quincy, CA reported storm total snow amounts of 16 to 22 inches. Lower Lassen Peak weather station reported 40 inches of storm total snow. Quincy COOP reported 20 inches of storm total snow, and Chester COOP reported 15 inches of snow. Gusty winds were observed with this storm, with 54 mph reported at Camel Peak, 35 mph reported at Humbug Summit RAWS, 45 mph reported at Colby Mountain RAWS, and 40 mph reported at Hatchet Mountain. Area power outages were reported.

A trained spotter at Sims reported a storm total snow of 36 inches at an elevation of 2800 feet. The National Operational Hydrologic Remote Sensing Center estimated 12 to 36 inches fell for storm total snow in the mountains of northern Shasta County. Interstate 5 northbound was closed at Fawndale due to winter weather conditions from 8:53 pm 2/23 to 1:00 am 2/24.

Low elevation snow fell over the northern Sacramento Valley. Snowfall reports included 6 inches at Red Bluff (300 feet), 6.5 inches for northern Redding (580 feet), 5 inches at Redding Fire (near Redding Airport), and 4 inches at Red Bluff water treatment. The National Operational Hydrologic Remote Sensing Center estimated 2 to 8 inches fell for storm total snow. Interstate 5 northbound was closed 10 miles north of Redding at Fawndale due to winter weather conditions from 8:53 pm 2/23 to 1:00 am 2/24.
Low elevation snow fell into the northeast foothills. Snowfall reports included 15 inches at Upper Magalia (2855 feet) and 11 inches at Paradise (2100 feet).

Low elevation snow fell into the Motherlode foothills. CoCoRaHS snowfall reports included 10.8 inches at Nevada City 3.4 NNW , and 10.5 inches at Nevada City 1.7 SSE, 7.7 inches of snow at Camino 1.2 N. Many schools and businesses were reported closed.

events.cz_name: MOUNTAINS SOUTHWESTERN SHASTA COUNTY TO WESTERN COLUSA COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The National Operational Hydrologic Remote Sensing Center estimated 6 to 18 inches fell for storm total snow in the mountains of southwestern County and western Colusa County.

More than 800 PG&E customers in the downtown area of Chico were without power on the afternoon of 2/21. The outage was between Main Street and Orange Street and between W. 1st Street and W. 7th Street. Some traffic lights were reported out. Winds at Chico Airport were sustained at 31 mph with gusts to 49.5 mph.
A power outage in Nevada City affected 1,278 customers on the east side of Hwy 20 and another 54 on Cement Hill.
There was 1 inch hail reported along Highway 45 just south of County Road 26, reported via Twitter.
There was 1-3 inches of hail accumulated over the roadway.
There was 0.75 inch hail reported in Chico, reported via Facebook.

Heavy snow fell over the northern Sierra. UC Berkeley Central Sierra Snow Lab reported 60.9 inches storm total snow. Caltrans reported storm total snow amounts of 40 inches at Castle Peak, but was unable to report measurements on the 6th due to road conditions. Ski resorts reported 44 inches at Kirkwood Mountain Resort, 32 inches at Sierra-at-Tahoe, 52 inches at Palisades Tahoe, and 73 inches at Sugar Bowl Resort. Caltrans reported the closure of mountain highways due to heavy snow and strong wind, including Interstate 80 and State Route 49 due to heavy blowing snow bringing very low visibility and causing multiple spinouts. Interstate 80 was closed from Colfax to the Nevada State Line at 1:15 pm on the 4th and remained closed for nearly 34 hours. Several ski resorts were closed due to heavy snow and whiteout conditions. Winds gusted to 40 to 60 mph. Local broadcast media reported the closure of numerous schools in the Sierra, with extensive power outages.

The COOP Observer in Quincy, CA reported 15 inches of snow by the morning of the 5th. A trained spotter in Quincy reported 17 inches of snow by the morning of the 5th, with a storm total snow amount of 29 inches. Lower Lassen Peak weather station reported 19.7 inches of storm total snow. Shingletown CoCoRaHS reported 6.9 inches of storm total snow, and Chester CoCoRaHS reported 11 inches of snow. Gusty winds were observed with this storm, with 44 mph reported at Cashman RAWS, 40 mph reported at Colby Mountain RAWS, and 44 mph reported at Saddleback RAWS. Widespread power outages were reported.

Accumulating snow fell into the Motherlode foothills. CoCoRaHS snowfall reports included 3.0 inches at Grass Valley 2.7 SW, and 2.5 inches at Sonora 3.4E, 3.5 inches at Volcano 3.2N and 5.8 inches of snow at Camino 1.2 N. Schools and businesses were reported closed. Numerous power outages were reported, including continued outages from previous storms. Several storage units collapsed in Grass Valley due to heavy snow load. No injuries reported.
The National Operational Hydrologic Remote Sensing Center estimated 4 to 6 inches of snow fell for a storm total in the Burney Basin.

Low elevation snow fell into the northeast foothills, with 2 to 6 inches estimated by National Operational Hydrologic Remote Sensing Center.
California Highway Patrol reported roadway flooding halfway into the slow lane on SR 99 near highway 50 eastbound junction due to heavy rain.
California Highway Patrol reported roadway flooding of lanes 3 and 4 on northbound I-5 just south of Highway 50 junction.
California Highway Patrol reported roadway flooding on Scott Road and Latrobe Road by Indian Creek.
Flooding near I-680 and Gold Hill Road offramp south of Cordelia is effecting southbound traffic on I-680.
Mudslide on SR 99 North and 6th onramp. Onramp closed.

The National Operational Hydrological Remote Sensing Center's gridded snowfall analysis estimated 4 to 18 inches over the Burney Basin and Eastern Shasta County over 72 hours.

The National Operational Hydrological Remote Sensing Center's gridded snowfall analysis estimated 6 to 24 inches over Shasta Lake and northern Shasta County over 72 hours. A trained spotter at Sims at an elevation of 2500 ft reported 14 inches in 24 hours. Caltrans reported the closure of Interstate 5 northbound at Fawndale for about 10 hours due to winter weather conditions.

events.cz_name: MOUNTAINS SOUTHWESTERN SHASTA COUNTY TO WESTERN COLUSA COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The National Operational Hydrological Remote Sensing Center's gridded snowfall analysis estimated 6 to 24 inches over the mountains of southwestern Shasta County to western Colusa County over 72 hours.

CoCoRaHS reported storm total amounts of 36 inches in Chester at 4526 ft, 38 inches at Meadow Valley at an elevation of 4380 ft, and 28 inches at Shingletown at an elevation of 3630 ft. The National Operational Hydrological Remote Sensing Center's gridded snowfall analysis estimated 12 to 36 inches over the Lassen Park and western Plumas County area over 72 hours. Lassen National Park reported 22 inches of snow.

Ski resorts reported storm total snow amounts of 23 inches at Kirkwood, 19 inches at Sugar Bowl, and 17 inches at Sierra at Tahoe. Caltrans District 3 reported storm total snow amounts of 23.5 inches at Kingvale, 21 inches at Soda Springs, and 18 inches at Eagle Lakes. The National Operational Hydrological Remote Sensing Center's gridded snowfall analysis estimated 6 to 30 inches over the west slope northern Sierra Nevada over 72 hours. 1 death was reported by broadcast media in Alta, CA where a man died from a collapsed snow bank, trapping him next to a generator and exposing him to carbon monoxide. Interstate 80 was closed intermittently on 3/28 due to winter weather conditions and multiple spinouts.

Reports on social media showed an estimated 2 inches of snow on the ground in Grass Valley with more snow falling. The National Operational Hydrological Remote Sensing Center's gridded snowfall analysis estimated 1 to 8 inches of storm total snow over portions of the the northeast foothills. CoCoRaHS reported 3.1 inches of snow near Nevada City at an elevation of 2390 ft, and 7 inches near Grass Valley at an elevation of 2782 ft.
The National Operational Hydrological Remote Sensing Center's gridded snowfall analysis estimated 1 to 4 inches over portions of the Motherlode.
The California Highway patrol reported flooding of Interstate 80 west of the Cisco Road onramp. There were also other various other reports of flooding of on and off ramps along Interstate 80.
The California Highway Patrol reported flooding near the Corral Hollow Rd and West Linne Road near the creek. Water was reported to be over the roadway.
The California Highway Patrol reported roadway flooding in both lanes of traffic along California Highway 4 at Bonanza Mine Way.
California Highway Patrol reported mud across Zogg Mine Road from heavy rain, blocking the entire roadway.
California Highway Patrol reported 3 feet of water along the Interstate 5 southbound onramp at Highway 299.
California Highway Patrol reported 1 foot of water in the roadway.
Spotter SO-47 reported rotation in a funnel cloud near Leisure Town Road and Alamo Drive.
The public reported hail, measured at 0.88 inches, associated with a thunderstorm.
The public reported 1 inch hail near Haille Road. The time was estimated by radar.
Strong straight-line winds downed multiple trees and utility poles near downtown Woodland. Sacramento International Airport reported a max gust of 46 mph. Time was estimated by radar.
The National Operational Hydrologic Remote Sensing Center estimated 8 to 30 inches of storm total snow. Lower Lassen Peak reported 13.2 inches of snow over 72 hours.

The UC Berkeley Central Sierra Snow Lab reported storm total amounts of 15.5 inches of snow, Bear Valley Resort reported 17 inches of storm total snow, Dodge Ridge Summit reported 36 inches of storm total snow, Kirkwood reported 20 inches of storm total snow, Sierra-at-Tahoe reported 21 inches of storm total snow, and Sugar Bowl Resort reported 19 inches of storm total snow.

San Joaquin County Sheriff issued evacuation orders for 2 locations along the San Joaquin River starting on March 19, 2023. Those two locations include Airport Court, Manteca and Haven Acres Marina in Lathrop due to heavy rain and snowmelt. Evacuation orders were lifted on April 11, 2023.

Flash flooding was reported in the downtown area of Sonora due to heavy rain from a severe thunderstorm. Tuolumne County OES reported a creek flowing out of banks, and water flowing over Washington Street, impacting approximately 25 to 30 homes, 10 public buildings and 30 businesses.
Calaveras County Sheriff Dispatch reported significant roadway flooding with two houses flooded in Copperopolis.
Tuolumne County Emergency Manager reported significant roadway flooding in the town of Tuolumne with creeks overflowing their banks.
California Highway Patrol in Stockton reported roadway flooding leading to the road closure near Filbert Street Off Ramp and Highway 4.
Caltrans District 10 reported a mudslide on State Route 49 between Fairview Lane and Mill Villa Court in Sonora due to heavy rain.
Law enforcement reported roadway flooding across all lanes at State Route 120 West and Interstate 5 South.
Caltrans District 2 initiated 24-hour traffic control on State Route 89 between Moccasin and Indian Falls due to heavy rain leading to a slide.
California Highway Patrol reported flooding near Twin Cities Road and Hardesty Lane.

Glenn County OES reported numerous road closures across the county due to flooding, including County Road FF from CR 9 to CR 200, County Road G from CR 9 to CR 200, County Road 25 from CR F to CR H, County Road 67 from CR Z to Butte County.
California Highway Patrol reported roadway flooding at Winding Way and Walnut Avenue, with the entire lane flooded.
Broadcast media reported roadway flooding between Fifield Road and Pleasant Grove Road.
California Highway Patrol reported roadway flooding near Flores Avenue.
California Highway Patrol reported roadway flooding between River Road and Chico River Road.
California Highway Patrol reported roadway flooding near Whitmore Road.
California Highway Patrol reported roadway flooding between Antelope Boulevard and Gilmore Road.
California Highway Patrol reported water overflowing the roadway and going into houses at Main Street and Trefoil Lane.
California Highway Patrol reported roadway flooding at the corner of Live Oak Road and Willard Road west of Red Bluff.
California Highway Patrol reported substantial flooding across the roadway, leading to the closure of the roadway near Gas Point Road and Park Drive.
California Highway Patrol reported substantial flooding across the roadway, leading to the closure of the roadway near Gas Point Road and Park Drive.
California Highway Patrol reported substantial flooding across the roadway, leading to the closure of the roadway near Gas Point Road and Park Drive.
Sacramento Fire reported a water rescue via rescue boats of two adults and a dog that were trapped inside of a makeshift shelter. No injuries.
Broadcast media reported mandatory evacuation orders for the commercial trailer park called Loveys Landing due to flooding near the Sacramento River.
California Highway Patrol reported roadway flooding at Dersch Road and Hyrax Road.
Tuolumne County Emergency Manager received multiple reports of a funnel cloud, observed along Campo Seco Road in Jamestown.
A National Weather Service employee as well as multiple reports on social media confirmed a funnel cloud east of Tracy at 1321 PDT. The time and location was estimated from radar.
The public reported hail with hail stones up to an inch in Stockton. Time was estimated from radar.
A trained spotter reported 1 inch hail in Downtown Sonora.
Numerous hardwood trees snapped or uprooted. A wooden power pole snapped in half.  NWS Storm Survey determined it to be rated EF-1 with 90 mph winds.

Tuolumne County Emergency Manager reported several trees and power poles down near the intersection of Martin Lane and Campo Seco Road. The Mount Elizabeth RAWS reported a maximum wind gusts of 61 mph.
Tuolumne County OES reported extensive tree damage at Woods Creek Mobile Home Park with 34 trees down.

Low elevation snow fell over the northern Sacramento Valley with significant accumulation into Redding. Snowfall reports included 7 inches at Happy Valley (900 feet), 6.0 inches for West Redding (500 feet), 5 inches at North Redding (500 feet), and 5 inches in southern Redding, in the city. Interstate 5 northbound was closed 10 miles north of Redding at Fawndale due to winter weather conditions from 5:29 pm 3/9 to 9:58 am 3/10.

Accumulated heavy snow from a series of storms caused the roof of a school in Nevada City to collapse. There was 3.6 inches of snow reported 2 NNW of Nevada City on the 8th, but this was in addition to previous snow and road from earlier storms.

Caltrans reported 13 inches of snow at Castle Peak, while Boreal Ski Resort reported 13 inches of snow and Central Sierra Snow Lab 10.6 inches. This brought chain controls and travel delays on Interstate 80 and US Highway 50.
There was 9.2 inches of snow measured at Lower Lassen Peak. Chester 0.9 NNE reported 8 inches of snow. Shingletown 2.5 NE reported 5.7 inches of snow.

Heavy snow fell over high elevations, impacting travel at Sierra passes, causing chain controls and slow downs. Bear Valley Ski Resort measured 15 inches on the morning of the 10th, with a storm total through the 15th of 30.5 inches. Kirkwood Ski Resort measured 15 inches on the morning of the 10th, with a storm total through the 15th of 29 inches. Sugar Bowl Ski Resort measured 12 inches on the morning of the 10th, with a storm total through the 15th of 29 inches.
Calaveras County Public Works reported the closure of Cooper Cove Drive between Black Creek Drive and Cheyenne Road in Copperopolis due to severe road damage by flooding.
The California Highway Patrol reported roadway flooding along southbound Interstate 505 offramp at County Road 19.
The California Highway Patrol reported mud, dirt and rock along the southbound lane of State Highway 49 near the SR 193 junction.
The California Highway Patrol reported a mudslide in the roadway between Old Auburn Foresthill Road and Mammoth Bar Road.
Kiefer Blvd closed at Highway 16 due to water on the roadway.
The California Highway Patrol reported a mudslide between China Gulch Drive and Canyon Road.
The California Highway Patrol reported flooding across SR 108 where the roadway dips down.
The California Highway Patrol reported water across the Interstate 5 on-ramp.
The California Highway Patrol reported water rushing across the roadway at Whitmore Road and Cow Creek Road.
The public reported hail up to quarter size along Highway 26 near Beyer Lane. Photos confirmed this. The Time was estimated by radar.

Glenn County completed a preliminary estimate of damage from heavy rainfall and flooding. There was substantial flooding, resulting in approximately $600,000 in damage to public infrastructure, including roads, bridges and culverts.
All public entities in Tuolumne County completed a preliminary estimate of storm damage for February through April, with costs well over $42 million.

Caltrans reported 10 inches of new snow at Castle Peak (7165 feet), 6 inches at Soda Springs (6819 feet) and 4 inches at Kingvale (6093 feet). UC Berkeley Central Sierra Snow Lab reported 6 inches (6894 feet). Sugar Bowl Ski Resort reported 9 inches of new snow at the summit (8383 feet). Sierra at Tahoe Ski resort reported 4 inches of new snow (8852 feet). Kirkwood Ski Resort reported 5 inches of new snow (7690 feet). The snow brought chain controls and delays on Interstate 80 and US Highway 50.

Sugar Bowl Ski Resort reported 7 inches of new snow at the summit (elevation 8383 feet) and 5 inches at the base (elevation 6640 feet). UC Berkeley reported 4.7 inches of new snow (elevation 6894 feet). Caltrans reported 4 inches of new snow at Castle Peak (elevation 7165 feet), 3 inches at Kingvale (elevation 6093 feet).

A 21-year-old man drowned in the Feather River after diving off of the Magalia Head Dam. His body was found down-stream the next day. Afternoon temperatures were 67-72 degrees, with water temperatures in the area ranging from 45-55 degrees that afternoon. Winds were 5-10 mph, and the West Branch Feather River - Magalia gauge flow was around 1540 cfs.

A 22-year-old woman drowned in the Clavey River on May 29th, with her body found downstream of Clavey Bridge on June 3rd. Warm weather was occurring with highs in the region in the lower 70s, while area waterways were cold with strong currents from mountain snowmelt.
Caltrans reported 8 inches of new snow at Soda Springs and Yuba Pass, 5 inches at Kingvale, Eagle Lakes and Blue Canyon. Central Sierra Snow Lab measured 8.3 inches.
Lower Lassen Peak (8234 feet) measured 5.2 inches of new snow. Quincy COOP observed 3.5 inches. Shingletown 2.5 E reported 0.7 inches.

A 20-year-old man drowned in the North Fork of the American River on May 14th, with his body found downstream in Lake Clementine on June 10th. Warm weather was occurring with highs in the region in the mid to upper 80s, while area waterways were cold with strong currents from mountain snowmelt.

A 15-year-old man drowned in the Sacramento River near Sand Cove Park on June 4th, with his body found on June 5th. Strong currents pulled him and 2 others downstream. A bystander in a boat nearby was able to rescue two. Warm weather was occurring with highs of 96 at downtown Sacramento, 94 at Sacramento Executive Airport reported. A Sacramento Fire Department Captain confirmed that high water levels with strong currents and cold water temperatures were observed during search efforts. Water temperatures in the general area at the time measured between 55 and 65 degrees.  The cold water and strong currents were due to unusually heavy mountain snowmelt.

There was a report of a lightning strike that hit a tree, causing a branch to penetrate the roof of the building in the Shasta View neighborhood in eastern Redding, next to Mountain View. No injuries were reported.
Heavy rain from thunderstorms produced a debris flow/ rock slide along Highway 70 at Serpentine Curves near Belden. This was reported by the California Highway Patrol.
The California Highway Patrol reported multiple slides mud/dirt/rock on SR 70 east of Twain, completely blocking the roadway.
The California Highway Patrol reported multiple mud/dirt/rock slides west of Hot Springs Ravine on SR 70/Feather River Scenic Byway.

The California Highway Patrol reported State Route 89 approximately 3 miles north of Greenville Wye was blocked due to a debris flow at 4:08 PM on June 12. The road was opened to one way traffic by 4:19 PM on June 12, and was fully cleared to through traffic by 7:01 AM on June 13.

The California Highway Patrol-Truckee reported the closure of portions of Donner Pass Road (Old Highway 40) due to a rock slide/large boulder in the road between Sugar Bowl and Truckee after thunderstorms brought locally heavy rain the day before.
Snow levels were near 3500 feet with one to two feet of snow falling above 5000 feet.  Southerly wind gusts reached 60 to 70 mph.

The Butte Lightning Complex (BTU) consisted of 34 fires ignited by lightning strikes on June 21st spread over 16,000 acres. There were 6 minor injuries to firefighters reported (see CA-Z066 entry), 2 structures destroyed, and 1200 residences threatened. Multiple evacuations and road closures were ordered. The fires extended into the northeast foothills of the Sierra Nevada (CA-Z066), where most of the fires and injuries were located.  The fires had only 25 percent containment by the end of the month and are continued in the July Storm Data entry.

The Butte Lightning Complex (BTU) consisted of 34 fires ignited by lightning strikes on June 21st and spread over 16,000 acres, extending into the central Sacramento Valley (CA-Z016). California Highway Patrol reported a downed tree on power lines on Meadow Ranch Road and Thatcher Mill Road with power lines lying across the roadway.

Mather Field Airport reported a wind gust of 68 mph. Sacramento International Airport reported a wind gust of 64 mph. McClellan Airfield reported sustained winds of 43 mph with gusts to 59 mph, and a max gust of 66 mph. Vacaville Nut Tree Airport reported a gust of 59 mph. Numerous reports of downed power lines and trees across the area, closing roads and damaging cars. Sacramento County OES reported two fatalities from fallen trees, over 200,000 power outages, roof damages to airport facilities, multiple downed trees and road and park closures. The City of Sacramento estimated $350,000 total combined cost for storm damage. Yolo County OES reported over 4,000 power outages, school closures, and downed trees.
Fairfield/Travis Air Force Base reported a max wind gust of 63 mph.

Stockton Airport reported a max gust of 60 mph. Modesto Airport reported a max gust of 55 mph. California Highway Patrol reported multiple power lines down, downed trees, and road closures. Stanislaus County OES reported short-term power outages from the high winds.

Local broadcast media reported the death of an elderly man that was killed when a large redwood tree fell on his home and crushed him. Around the time of the report, Marysville Airport reported a gust of 53 mph. Yuba County Airport reported a wind gust of 68 mph at 6:29 pm, about an hour later. Oroville Airport reported a max wind gust of 70 mph. Sutter County OES reported 4 schools closed with over 11,000 customers without power and proclaimed a local emergency. Butte County OEM proclaimed a local emergency due to wind damage, as hundreds of trees were downed leading to outages, road closures, and property damage.

California Highway Patrol reported numerous downed trees and power lines due to high wind. A station in Placerville recorded a max gust of 64 mph. Nevada County Air Park reported a max gust of 52 mph. Calaveras Airport reported a max gust of 51 mph. Calaveras County OES reported scattered power outages throughout the county, removal of 55 downed trees from county roads, and 1 tree on a home. Tuolumne County OES reported multiple downed trees along roadways. Nevada County OES reported widespread power outages and downed trees across roads and into structures,  with moderate impacts to telecommunications. El Dorado County OES reported 40 calls for service related to trees and wires down, at least 5 buildings struck by trees, and 1 uninjured person trapped in a mobile home from a tree on top of the home.

Redding Municipal Airport reported a max gust of 55 mph. Red Bluff Airport reported a max gust of 51 mph. California Highway Patrol reported downed powerlines touching the roadway at Lee Street and Clara Court.
Jarbo Gap RAWS reported a max gust of 75 mph. Cohasset RAWS reported a max gust of 62 mph.  California Highway Patrol reported a downed tree and powerlines along Cement Hill Road and Gochine Drive.
Sutter County OES reported the closure of Highway 99 to Highway 113 due to flooding from heavy rain. At least 5 other roads were closed within the county.

Stanislaus County OES reported the closure of Montpelier Road from Keyes to Whitmore due to flooding. At least 8 other roads within the county were closed due to flooding. Minor street and residential flooding were also reported.

Glenn County OES reported the closure of Willows-Glenn County Airport taxiway and runway due to flooding and debris, with damage to the shoulder. Damage, culvert failure, and temporary closure of multiple county roads. There were 8 water rescues within the county as well with this event. The Glenn County Landfill infrastructure was also damaged from flooding and erosion.

California Highway Patrol and Placer County OES reported a fatality of a driver that drove through standing water on a flooded road, lost control, and flipped the vehicle, coming to a rest in standing water on Nicolaus Road near Marcum Road.

On May 9th, a 30 year old female was watching her children play in the water and noticed her 11 year old daughter struggling to keep her head above water. The 30 year old female then jumped into the river to help, but also struggled to stay afloat. Soon after seeing this, her 14 year old son then jumped in the water to help. The 14 year old and 11 year old were able to make it safely back to shore, but the 30 year old female did not. At 6:30 PM on May 9th, a 911 call was received for a water rescue in the San Joaquin River. Then, at 5:30 PM on May 11th, the body of the 30 year old female was recovered in the San Joaquin River by a volunteer diver. Water temperatures in the mid 60s to low 70s between Crows Landing and Hills Ferry over the weekend. San Joaquin River - Newman gage indicated river stage around 51.8 feet on May 9th at 5 PM, with stage gradually rising to 53.8 feet by Saturday, May 11th at 6:45 PM.

On May 12th just after noon, a swimmer was pulled from the confluence of the American River near Auburn after emergency personnel responded for reports of a drowning. The woman who was missing in the water was found and responders attempted medical aid but she succumbed to her injuries. Water temperatures in the area were in the mid to upper 50s. A nearby gauge at the North Fork Dam observed stage at 2.35 feet with a flow rate of 1,994 cfs as of 8:15 am PDT in the morning.

A swimmer was swimming in the Woodward Reservoir across the channel near Mountain View Point on May 25th, 2024 and was found dead after he went under the water and never came back up. Authorities found his body around 8pm. Water Temperature at Stanislaus River at Oakdale CA, approximately 5 miles from the Woodward Reservoir, was 53-57 degrees between the hours of 6 AM and 9 PM. Water Temperature at Stanislaus River at Orange Blossom Bridge, approximately 6 miles from the Woodward Reservoir, was 52-57 degrees between the hours of 6 AM and 9 PM. Max temperature for Modesto Airport, approximately 15 miles away, was 76 degrees on May 25th, 2024.
A lightning strike resulted in a mobile home fire around 6:15 pm PDT on Nob Hill Drive in the Castle City Mobile Home Park. The mobile home was destroyed. There were no injuries.

An adult male in his 30s went missing from a large party that was rafting down the American River toward Rossmoor Bar around 11:29 AM on Saturday, June 15th, 2024. The man was not wearing a life jacket and was swept underwater, last seen at Clay Banks. Numerous resources were called to search, including firefighters, a Sacramento Metro Fire helicopter and search party, Sacramento Drowning Accident Rescue Team (DART), and Sacramento County Sheriff's Office. His body was recovered in the morning, on Sunday, June 16th, 2024. Broadcast media reported that a sizable Sierra snowpack has led to river levels that are higher and faster than usual for this time of year, and that recent flows on the river at Fair Oaks were measured as fast as 3,600 cubic feet per second, twice the mean average for this time of year, according to the U.S. Geological Survey. Water temperature observations nearby showed temperatures in the upper 50s to low 60s around the general area.

Crews responded to the report of a possible drowning at Lake Clementine Trail before 5:30 p.m on June 25th, 2024. A communications manager for California State Parks said three people had attempted to swim across the river and were swept downstream by the current. A 33-year-old man was found dead in the water, the El Dorado County Sheriff's Office said. Officials said a 15-year-old boy was found, and CPR was performed by State Parks lifeguards and Cal Fire. He was taken to Sutter Auburn Faith Hospital where he later died. State parks said another teenage male was pulled from the water and was uninjured. Water temperatures were in the low to mid 60's.

The Aero Fire started in the afternoon on June 17th, 2024 near Rock Creek Road and Highway 4, near Copperopolis. The cause was under investigation, and spread over 5000 acres within the first 24 hours due to strong northerly winds and low relative humidity. Northerly winds were around 10 to 20 mph sustained with gusts of 25 to 35 mph were observed, with minimum relative humidity around 20 to 25 percent. The fire reached 5285 acres but was 100 percent contained by June 27th, 2024. 1 structure was damaged, and 3 were destroyed.

events.event_narrative: The Sites Fire started on June 17th, 2024 in the afternoon and spread rapidly, especially within the first 24 hours due to strong and gusty northerly winds and low relative humidity. Relative humidity fell to the single digits on June 17th, and remained very dry through the 18th. The fire grew rapidly during these 2 days through grass and brush. Minimal growth was observed afterwards. The fire cause was under investigation, and was 100% contained on June 28th, with a final size of 19,195 acres.

The Thompson Fire started around 11 am on July 2nd, 2024 near the spillway of Lake Oroville Dam. Very hot temperatures combined with critical fire weather conditions allowed for rapid growth of the fire shortly after ignition prompting several evacuation warnings and orders. Within the first 24 hours, the fire was mapped at over 3,000 acres. The California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (Cal Fire) reported the fire to be 100% contained on July 8th, 2024 at 3,789 acres. Red Flag conditions were not being met at the time of ignition, however temperatures reached around 100 to 104 degrees, with relative humidity in the 10 to 18 percent range, and wind gusts of 20 to 25 mph. From July 3rd through 8th, the heat continued with temperatures peaking around 110 to 115 degrees, and low relative humidity continued, in the 8 to 18 percent range, however winds returned to more of the typical diurnal regime. Over 10,000 people were under evacuation orders. The California Department of Water Resources activated the EAP for Lake Oroville Dam under non-emergency level. The fire resulted in loss of transmission lines. 8 structures were damaged, and 26 structures were destroyed.
Weather stations in the area reported daytime high temperatures of 90 to 100 degrees across this zone, with overnight lows in the 60s to low 70 degree range from June 4th through June 6th.

The Park Fire began the month at 22% contained with 393,012 acres. During the first half of the month, above normal temperatures and elevated fire weather conditions continued active spread and activity. Afternoon highs ranged from 82 to 104 with dry conditions of minimum humidities ranging from 10-25%. Rapid acre growth tapered off after August 8th, reaching 427,067 acres, 34% containment, 636 structures destroyed. ||Conditions cooled to normal to below normal temperatures with seasonal fire weather conditions, including scattered rain showers, allowing for lowered fire activity. Temperatures ranged from mid 70s to mid 90s with containment at 79% and total acres at 429,603. By the end of the month, 709 Structures have been destroyed with 54 damaged. Currently, minimal fire activity is reported, well within the fire perimeter. An IMET remains deployed to the fire and is tasked through mid September.

The Crozier Fire started in the night on August 7th, 2024 and was discovered at 1:21 AM. It burned actively for the first two days in steep, rugged timber and in dry fuels. The fire burned a total of 1,960 acres and was reported 100% contained on August 20th.  Evacuation orders were in place for Garden Valley, Georgetown, Volcanoville, Mosquito, Quintette, and Swansboro areas. Evacuation warnings were in place for areas to the east and southwest of the fire. Seasonably hot temperatures, low relative humidity, and locally breezy wind gusts of up to 10-20 mph were observed during the initial spread. Daytime highs in the 90s to around 100 degrees were observed during the active burning periods, with daytime relative humidity in the low teens and poor overnight recoveries around 20-30%.

A brief EF-0 tornado touched down at 2 ENE Salida at 2:13 PM PDT and was on the ground for 0.9 miles until 2:15 PM PDT. The tornado moved through several orchards and 3 properties. Dozens of almond trees were uprooted and large tree branches were broken. Minor structure damage observed at the properties included a covered patio and roof material ripped off, a broken window, and outbuilding and metal fencing was displaced, and a large trailer was lifted and moved approximately 20 feet.

Placer County Sheriff Office dive team discovered a body in the American River Sunday, May 18th, 2025 around 3 PM PDT in the Oregon Bar area of the river. Water temperatures at the time of body discovery were in the low 60s.

Local broadcast media shared information that crews found the body of a missing 23 year old fisherman who went into the water to cool down. He was walking in the river at waist level when he hit a drop off and was pulled underwater and struggled to swim. He went under the surface and never came back up. He was not wearing a life jacket. Water temperatures at the time were estimated to be between 65 and 70 degrees. The drowning occurred in Yolo County on the Sacramento River near Old River Road and Levee Road.

A weather system brought a brief period of moderate snow showers that led to multiple spinouts and a jackknifed big rig. These accidents resulted in the closure of I-80 westbound at Truckee. Traffic was initially stopped at 4:46 PM PDT but was then closed from 4:56 PM PDT through 7:54 PM PDT. Chain restrictions were in effect for trucks for most of the day. UC Berkeley Central Sierra Snow Lab measured 5.9 inches of snow in 24 hours at 6894 feet.

Lightning from a mix of wet and dry thunderstorms in the area led to the ignition of the Green Fire in Shasta Trinity National Forest on July 1st, 2025. A period of very hot and dry weather followed that allowed for the fire to spread. Periodically breezy diurnal winds also aided in the spread of the fire. As of July 31st, the fire sits at a 92% containment and 19,022 acres. Evacuation warnings were issued in the surrounding areas as a result.

The TCU September Lightning Complex began as a series of lightning fire starts on the morning of September 2nd across 4 counties, Calaveras, San Joaquin, Stanislaus and Tuolumne. The largest fires are the 6-5 fire and the 2-7 fire, with total acreage burned at 13,966 Acres. There has been 1 firefighter injury reported, with 85 structures destroyed and 6 damaged, including structures in the historic Gold Rush town of China Camp. Numerous roads were closed including both sides of Highway 120 from Chinese Camp to Highway 120 Bridge, all Roads east of Highway 108 from J-59 to Highway 120, as well as portions of Highway 49 and Highway 108 in the area. The fire was declared 100 percent contained on September 13.

It was determined that this caused a downburst of strong straight-line winds. Sporadic wind damage to trees and powerlines was noted along with several large mature trees that were uprooted and fell into homes. The damage swath was 2.5 miles long and 1.5 miles wide from American River College, northeast in the vicinity of a line from East Lawn Mortuary to Mercy San Juan Medical Center. Law enforcement reported several debris flows on Highways 32 and 36 due to heavy rain over areas that burned earlier in the year.

Cal Fire reported numerous debris flows on Highway 70 due to heavy rain over adjacent areas burned earlier in the year. Several of the flows were located between their fire station and the Pulga Bridge. Cleanup was finished at 1000PST.

Rainfall near a burn area west of Redding brought debris onto the road. The California Highway Patrol reported a car being hit by rocks from a slide west of Redding. The rockslide was near mile marker 35 on Highway 299 at 11:21PST. A boulder fell in the westbound lane of Highway 299 just west of Big Flat Campground at 13:41PST.
A new daily rainfall record of 0.17 inches was set at Sacramento Executive Airport. This broke the old record of 0.03 inches set in 1993.
A new daily rainfall record of 0.46 inches was set at Modesto Airport. This broke the old record of 0.41 inches set in 1994.

The California Highway Patrol reported multiple locations of rock and mud debris on Highway 70 near Yankee Rd and the town of Concow. A wildfire had burned this area earlier in the year, making it susceptible to debris slides.

A new daily low temperature record of 37 degrees was set at Stockton Airport at 06:17PST, breaking the previous record of 42 degrees set in 1977.||A new daily low temperature record of 40 degrees was set at Modesto Airport at 06:22LST, breaking the previous record of 41 degrees set in 1981.

Rain caused damage to the Lodi Middle School administration building. The building was undergoing roof repairs, and a temporary tarp was in place. The tarp failed, allowing rain to enter the building and resulting in more than $100,000 damage.

Storms brought strong wind, low visibility, and heavy snow to the higher mountain elevations with most of the snow falling above 6000 feet. Fourteen inches of snow were reported at the Lassen Volcanic National Park Visitor Center, located at 6300 feet. Winds gusting to 45 mph were recorded at the Sugarloaf RAWS on November 1st at 0451PST. Heavy rain fell at lower elevations.

Heavy snow fell from several back-to-back storm systems, with snow levels beginning at above 8000 feet and gradually lowering below pass levels as colder air moved in. Fourteen inches of snow were reported at Castle Peak, 12-15 inches at Donner Summit, and 10-14 inches at Alpine Meadows.
A daily high temperature record of 77 degrees was tied at Modesto Airport.  The record was previously reached in 1995.

Snow amounts of 1 to 2 feet were common across the mountains, with as much as 3 to 5 feet in the ski resort areas near the Sierra Nevada crest. Echo Peak at 7670 feet received 24 inches of snow. Ebbetts Pass at 8700 feet had 35 inches of snow. Gusty winds and blowing snow brought very hazardous travel conditions to Interstate 80... Highway 50 and other mountain roads.

Snow amounts of 12 to 20 inches were common across the mountain commmunities. Snow levels were unusually low, with Quincy at 3420 feet elevation receiving 14 inches of snowfall. Lower Lassen Peak at 8250 feet recorded 45 inches of snowfall. Gusty winds combined with falling snow to produce occasional whiteout conditions.
A winter storm brought snow accumulations of 8 to 12 inches above elevations of 3000 feet and was accompanied by gusty winds. This brought hazardous travel conditions to area roads.
A winter storm brought snow accumulations of 6 to 12 inches to elevations above 3000 feet accompanied by strong, gusty winds. This brought hazardous travel conditions to area roads.

A winter storm brought snow accumulations of 6 to 12 inches with gusty winds to elevations above 3000 feet. Greater snow amounts fell above 6000 feet. Lassen Volcanic National Park measured 67 inches of snow at Lower Lassen Peak, which is at an elevation of 8250 feet. This brought hazardous travel conditions to eastern Shasta County, western Plumas County, and Lassen Volcanic National Park, with chain restrictions on Highways 299 and 44.

A winter storm brought snow accumulations of 2 to 3 feet to elevations above 7000 feet accompanied by strong, gusty winds. Snow amounts of a foot or more fell above 6000 feet, with several inches falling at elevations between 3000 and 6000 feet. Blue Canyon received 19 inches of snow, and Echo Peak measured 24 inches. This brought hazardous travel conditions and chain restrictions to area roads such as I-80 and US Highway 50. ||A woman was struck by a train on the 25th while hiking with her son on railroad tracks near Soda Springs. Whiteout conditions and snow accumulation made them unaware they were on railroad tracks. She died in a hospital in Truckee from her injuries. Her son was also injured.
A winter storm brought snow accumulations of 8 to 12 inches to elevations above 4000 feet accompanied by strong, gusty winds. This brought hazardous travel conditions to area roads.

events.event_narrative: A winter storm brought snow accumulations of 6 to 12 inches to elevations above 3000 feet accompanied by strong, gusty winds. This brought hazardous travel conditions to area roads.

Light winds and clear skies brought cold morning temperatures to the northern Sacramento Valley. The minimum temperature of 28 degrees tied the daily record at Redding Airport, which was previously set in 1998.
Sunny skies and a warming airmass allowed temperatures to tie the daily record high of 72 degrees at Red Bluff Airport. This record was previously set in 1976.
A daily low temperature record of 23 degrees was set at Redding Airport. This broke the old record of 24 degrees set in 1989.

A California Highway Patrol officer observed a funnel cloud form in a wall cloud and drop down on a farm around 3:00 pm PST. The tornado ripped most of the tin roof panels off of a 70 year old barn and also from a chicken coop. Roof pieces were found in a tree and in adjacent fields up to one half of a mile away. One tin roof piece shorted out power lines, causing a loss of power to the neighborhood. A pickup truck suffered damage to the driver side mirror from flying debris. Netting from pheasant pens was ripped up. A large steel hopper was knocked over. The farmhouse was undamaged and the farm animals were apparently unharmed. ||The tornado was non-supercellular and formed when a line of eastward moving thunderstorms ahead of a cold front collided with a westward moving thunderstorm. Neighbors 2 miles away in Princeton took photos of the tornado touching down in a burned rice field briefly before it went aloft and then dropped down on the barn. The tornado was reported to have touched down again just across the street in a field, dropping panels from the barn roof. Another funnel cloud was also reported which did not touch down.
A winter storm brought heavy snow and strong winds to the Mt Shasta and western Plumas County area.
A winter storm brought heavy snow and strong winds to the west slope of the northern Sierra Nevada Mountains.
A winter storm moved through northern Shasta County.
