A member of the public reported a brief funnel cloud between Orland and Hamilton City.
A tree was reported down, blocking SR12 at Double Springs Road. Unknown time of occurrence.

Caltrans reported a 24 hour total of 11 of new snow at Kingvale Maintenance Yard. Chain controls and slowdowns were reported on mountain portions of I80 and Highway 50. Bear Valley Ski Resort measured 8 of snow. A spotter at Camino at 3120 feet measured 3 of new snow over 24 hours. A spotter reported some wet snow falling at 2500 feet, with no accumulation.

A powerful Pacific storm brought wind gusts of 65 mph to the Cohasset RAWS automated weather station, which is located 12 miles northwest of Paradise. Numerous buildings were damaged due directly to the wind and/or to flying debris and falling trees and branches.  Hundreds of customers were without power for up to seven days.
Hail covered the ground to a depth of just over 2 inches. Most of the hail was pea size, but the larger hailstones were as large as nickels and quarters. The hail for about 15 minutes.
Hail as large as nickels was reported.

A lightning strike in Oakdale ignited a fire in several Italian cypress trees. The flames spread to nearby vegetation and then to a mobile home, which sustained moderate damage. A second mobile home sustained minor heat damage.

A 21 year old man drowned when he jumped off an embankment in Ripon on the Stanislaus River, he went under and water and didn't come up.  The Stanislaus River, was running fast and cold from the winter rains and melting of snow in the mountains. His body was found by the Ripon Fire Department on May 10th.
The Apple Fire in Tehama County (Off Apple Rd & Paskenta Rd, west of Corning), burned 2,956 acres with 3 residential structures and 2 outbuilding destroyed. The fire was contained by June 14.
The Pawnee Fire in Lake County (Pawnee Rd & New Long Valley Rd, northeast of Clearlake Oaks), burned 15,185 acres with 22 structures destroyed and 1 injury. The fire was contained by July 8.

The County Fire in Yolo and Napa counties (east of Lake Beryessa), burned 90,288 acres with 20 structures destroyed and 1 injury. The fire was started by an improperly installed electric livestock fence unit. The fire was contained on July 17.
The Chrome Fire in Glenn County (Hwy 162 and Forest Hwy 7, north of Elk Creek), burned 2,290 acres with 1 outbuilding destroyed. The fire was contained on June 21.

The Carr Fire began on the afternoon of July 23, 2018, at the intersection of Highway 299 and Carr Powerhouse Road, near French Gulch in Shasta County. The fire is reported to have been started accidentally by a vehicle towing a trailer that had a tire blow out, causing the steel rim to scrape along the pavement, generating sparks that ignited dry vegetation along the edge of the highway. Local winds generated by the fire are reported to have caused the fire to spread quickly.||At the end of July, the fire was the sixth most destructive fire in California history at 112,888 acres, with 1,378 structures destroyed, 965 of them homes. The fire was not fully contained until August 30, reaching 229,651 acres in size with a total of 1,079 residences, 22 commercial structures, 503 outbuildings destroyed. There were also 190 residences, 26 commercial structures, and 61 outbuildings damaged. About 38,000 people were evacuated from their homes. There were a total of 8 deaths from the fire, 3 of them firefighters. A large fire whirl in Redding has been reported as being responsible for 4 of the deaths, and this has been listed as a separate event. Damage costs to insured buildings are estimated at $1.5 billion for the Carr Fire.

A powerful fire whirl developed within the Carr Fire in western Redding, CA on July 26th, with winds estimated in excess of 143 mph, equivalent to an EF3 tornado. The fire whirl was estimated to be on ground from 7:30���8:00 p.m. The fire whirl caused extensive tornado-like damage while rapidly spreading the fire. The winds crumpled high tension electrical transmission towers, damaged homes, and debarked and uprooted trees. Wind damaged areas included locations untouched by fire, and included signs of ground scouring. The damage path was 2 miles long, with an estimated width of about half a mile. Three people were killed inside their Redding home after the structure's walls were blown out and the roof collapsed on the occupants. Several other homes suffered significant roof damage. A firefighter was killed while driving his vehicle near the fire whirl. Three bulldozers were impacted by flying debris, rocks, embers, smoke and intense heat, with the operators suffering injuries including burns and cuts from broken glass.

events.event_narrative: The Mendocino Complex Fire (made up of the River and Ranch Fires) spread across Colusa County, Glenn County, Lake County, and Mendocino County, becoming the largest wildfire in California history at 459,123 acres. The Mendocino Complex Fire was not contained until September 18. There were 157 residential buildings destroyed, 123 others destroyed. In addition, there were 13 residential buildings and 24 other buildings damaged. The fires caused at least $56 million in insured property damage. The city of Lakeport, communities of Kelseyville, Lucerne, Upper Lake, Nice, Saratoga Springs, Witter Springs, Potter Valley, and Finley, parts of Hopland, and the tribal communities of Hopland Rancheria and Big Valley Rancheria were evacuated. There was 1 firefighter killed (on August 13), 4 firefighters were injured.
Heavy rain from an isolated thunderstorm brought a rock slide covering the west bound lane of Highway 70. Radar estimates suggested locally 0.45 of rain within 1 hour.

The Donnell Fire began on August 1, 2018, along Highway 108 in Stanislaus National Forest in Tuolumne County. The cause of the fire is unknown. The fire burned 36,450 acres, 54 structures destroyed and 81 minor structures destroyed. of them homes. Among the destroyed buildings was the historic Dardanelle Resort and Dardanelle Bridge. The fire was not fully contained until early October. There were a total of 9 injuries from the fire.

The Hirz Fire began on August 9, 2018, near Lakehead by Shasta Lake, in Shasta-Trinity National Forest in Shasta County. The fire was determined to be human caused. The fire burned 46,150 acres and caused evacuations through the area, but no structures were destroyed and no injuries were reported. The fire was not fully contained until September 12. The fire came close to the Carr Fire. The Delta Fire burned into the western perimeter of the Hirz Fire on September 10.

The Delta Fire began on September 5, 2018, near Lakehead by Shasta Lake, in Shasta-Trinity National Forest in Shasta County. The fire was determined to be human caused. The fire burned 63,100 acres and caused evacuations through the area, with 20 structures destroyed and no injuries reported. The fire was not fully contained until October 7. The fire came close to the Carr Fire. The Delta Fire burned into the western perimeter of the Hirz Fire on September 10.

Emergency Manager relayed a report of a creek beginning to flood a barn near the Mendocino-Lake County border. The water was black from ash in the Mendocino Complex and higher than the resident had ever seen before.

The Camp Fire began on the morning of November 8, 2018, by Camp Creek Road, near Pulga in Butte County. The fire was not fully contained until November 25. This fire was the most destructive wildfire in California history, destroying much of the city of Paradise, the community of Concow, and damaging the towns of Pulga and Magalia. There were 18,804 structures destroyed, 13,696 of them single homes, along with 514 commercial structures and 3,718 outbuildings and 153,336 acres burned. There were a total of 86 deaths from the fire, with 12 civilians and 5 firefighters injured. There were 3 people missing as of 1/24/2019, when Butte County Sheriff closed their missing persons call center for the Camp Fire. Damage costs to insured buildings has been estimated to be at least $10 billion. |Conditions which lead to this fire included several recent years with drought conditions, late spring rainfall bringing additional growth of grass for fuel, dry weather for seven months prior to the fire, very low humidity due to several north wind events, record dry fuel and gusty northeast winds the day of the fire. Local wind gusts to 40 to 50 mph were measured nearby at Jarbo Gap, with a peak gust in the early morning of 52 mph. These winds caused the fire to spread very quickly. The fire forced the rapid evacuation of over 27,000 people from Paradise, Magalia, Centerville, Concow, Pulga, Butte Creek Canyon, Berry Creek and Yankee Hill. The fire also threatened the communities of Butte Valley, Chico, Forest Ranch, Helltown, Inskip, Oroville, and Stirling City. All residents were not allowed to return home until December 15, when the final evacuation orders were lifted. |Smoke from the fire was dense at times across much of Northern California, concentrated by strong atmospheric inversions. Air quality was reported by the Air Resources Board as some of the worst on record, causing many schools to close and events to be canceled across the area. Visibility was below 1/2 mile at times.|The cause of the fire is under investigation, though there evidence suggests it occurred near damaged power lines.
Roadway flooding at 4th St. and Hekman Circle. A vehicle was stalled on a flooded road.
A vehicle was stuck in a flooded roadway at West Colony Rd. and Calhoun Ave.
Roadway flooding was reported on Doak Blvd and South Mohler Rd and on Grange Way.
Off ramp at Penryn Rd. at I80 was partially blocked due to flooding.
All three lanes of Highway 99 and Highway 120 off ramp were flooded.
Both lanes on North Sierra Drive were flooded.
There was 1.41 of rain measured over 24 hours by a weather spotter in Loomis.
Dense smoke dropped visibilities down to a mile or less across across the southern Sacramento Valley. Air quality measurements were in the Unhealthy to Very Unhealthy range.
Dense smoke dropped visibilities down to a mile or less across across the northern Sacramento Valley. Air quality measurements were in the Unhealthy to Very Unhealthy range.
Dense smoke dropped visibilities down to a mile or less across across the northern San Joaquin Valley. Air quality measurements were in the Unhealthy range.

The Butte County Office of Education closed all public schools in the county through Friday, Nov. 23. Chico State University suspended classes until Monday, Nov. 26.

More than a foot of snow fell above 6500 feet over the the northern Sierra, bringing travel delays and chain controls on mountain highways such as I80 and Highway 50. This occurred during the busy Thanksgiving holiday. Highways over seasonal passes were closed, including SR-4 over Ebbetts Pass, SR-89 over Monitor Pass, and SR-108 over Sonora Pass. Kirkwood Ski Resort measured a total of 25 through the event at an elevation of 9800', while most ski peaks saw a little more than a foot. The Heavenly Ski Resort closed on Thanksgiving due to the snow.

About a foot of snow fell in the Lassen National Park area, bringing travel delays and closing the park road. This occurred during the busy Thanksgiving holiday. Lower Lassen Peak SNOTEL reported 11 of new snow, the first significant accumulation of the season. Manzanita Lake Campground closed due to the snow.

Heavy snow impacted mountain travel over Sierra passes, with snow totals of nearly 4 feet. Caltrans reported a storm total of 46 of snow measured by Castle Peak along I-80. Kirkwood Ski Resort reported 46, Squaw Alpine 45, Bear Valley 25, Kyburz had 10, with 1 down to Camino, elevation 3100'.
Heavy snow impacted mountain travel with delays and chain controls. There was 32 of snow reported at Lower Lassen Peak.

There were 10 slides into drainage systems along SR70, withing the Camp Fire burned area. The Concow/Pulga area was still under a mandatory evacuation order due to the Camp Fire. An automated gage at Durham reported very heavy rain from 1-2 pm of 1.64 and a second hour between 2-3 pm of 1.80.

The Butte County Sheriff's Office issued an evacuation order for Honey Run Road due to flooding, from the 200 block to Skyway including Horse Run Lane. Nearly 100 cars were trapped for at least an hour on Honey Run Road, as two separate debris flows and flooding blocked cars from evacuating safely. Officials from the Butte County Sheriff���s Office confirmed the backup was up to two miles long. An automated gage at Durham reported very heavy rain from 1-2 pm of 1.64 and a second hour between 2-3 pm of 1.80.||Water rescuers were later called out to Honey Run Road in the lower area of Butte Creek Canyon after a white Jeep Cherokee was reported floating down Butte Creek. |The U.S. Army mobilized 19 high water vehicles to rescue the people who were trapped. Evacuation warnings were in place for the Hamlin Canyon and Lower Neal zones, and on the west side of the county at Hegan Lane south to Highway 162 to the Sacramento River.

Flooding caused traffic delays and one hour of road closures on northbound and southbound Highway 99 from Neal Road to Estates Drive in Chico. Sheetflow was reported from heavy rain off of recently burned areas from the Camp Fire.

High wind was recorded across the area including a 69 mph wind gust at  Yuba City, a 66 mph wind gust at Chico airport, and a 61 mph wind gust at Marysville airport. A Yuba County employee was killed along Griffith Avenue just south of North Beale Road in Linda when he was struck by a falling eucalyptus tree branch while clearing roads of debris. There were many power outages due to power poles down from fallen trees and hundreds of customers were without power for up to seven days. Fallen trees and branches and flying debris also damaged cars and buildings. Sutter County Regional Airport had hangar and plane damage.

A 71 mph gust was measured 4 miles west northwest of Elk Grove. A 69 mph wind gust was measured at Sacramento Executive Airport and a 66 mph wind gust was measured at Sacramento International Airport. The State Legislature building had several windows broken and proceedings were  forced to be suspended. Many trees were reported down, including an 80 foot oak tree near the interesection of Elm and Hazel in Sacramento. PG&E reported many power poles down throughout the area and thousands of residents and businesses were without power for up to seven days. Several big rigs were reported down by the CHP, including one on I-5 south of River Rd. in Woodland, and another on I-80 east of State Route 113.

A 60 mph gust was measured at Suisun City, at the Travis Air Force Base. A roof was blown off of a building in Rio Vista and numerous other facilities were damaged due directly to the wind or from flying debris and falling trees and branches.

A 60 mph gust was recorded at Stockton Airport.  CHP reported an overturned big rig in Stockton on Lower Sacramento Rd. just south of 8 Mile Rd. A 44 mph gust was recorded in Modesto. Numerous homes and business facilities were damaged due ditrectly to the wind and/or by flying debris and falling trees and branches.

events.cz_name: MOUNTAINS SOUTHWEST SHASTA COUNTY TO NORTHERN LAKE COUNTY
events.event_narrative: A 65 mph wind gusts was recorded 18 miles south southeast of Saddle Camp.  Numerous buildings were damaged due directly to the wind and/or to flying debris and falling trees and branches.  Power was out to many customers for up to a day.

An 82 mph gust was recorded at the Redding RAWS automated weather station.  A 70 mph gust was measured at Redding Airport.  A 67 mph gust was recorded at Red Bluff Airport. Numerous buildings were damaged due directly to the wind and/or from flying debris and falling trees and branches.

A 73 mph gust was measured at the Lyons Valley RAWS automated weather station, 10 miles northwest of Lakeport.  Numerous buildings were damaged due directly to the wind and/or to flying debris and falling trees and branches.  Power was out to many customers for up to a day.

A spotter in Nevada City reported a gust to 92 mph on his weather station. He also reported numerous 3 foot diameter white fir and cedar trees down in the vicinity of Banner Mountain and the Maryland Rd. and Idaho Rd. intersection. A 70 mph gust was reported by Read Ranch RAWS automated weather station, located 7 miles northwest of Nevada City. Numerous buildings were damaged due directly to the wind and/or to flying debris and falling trees and branches.  Power was out to thousands of customers for up to seven days.

A 75 mph wind was reported at the Pike County Lookout RAWS automated weather staion, which is 2 miles southeast of Brush Creek Reservoir. Numerous buildings were damaged due directly to the wind and/or to flying debris and falling trees and branches.  Power was out to hundreds of customers for up to seven days.

A 72 mph wind gust was reported at Blue Canyon. Numerous buildings were damaged due directly to the wind and/or to flying debris and falling trees and branches.  Hundreds of customers were without power for up to seven days.
Rainfall at Red Bluff airport totaled 2.14 inches on January 25th, which|broke the previous record for the date of 1.38 inches set in 1997.
Heavy rain from a strong Pacific system resulted in a new daily rainfall record of 0.70 inches at the Stockton airport on January 5th. This breaks the old record of 0.69 inches set in 1992.
A strong Pacific storm resulted in a new daily rainfall record of 1.21 inches at Modesto on January 5th. This broke the old record of 0.79 inches set in 1995.

The high temperature in Stockton reached 72 degrees.  This broke the previous daily record high temperature of 70 degrees set in 1952.||The high temperature in Modesto reached 75 degrees.  This broke the previous daily record high temperature of 73 degrees set in 1992.
The temperature dropped to 35 degrees at the Stockton Airport this morning.  This tied the daily record originally set in 1987.
The temperature dropped to 34 degrees at the Stockton Airport this morning.  This broke the daily record of 35 degrees set in 1977.

Storms with heavy rain caused mudslides and debris flows on Highway 70 in the Pulga area. Debris flows clogged drains along the roadway. Trees along on roadway had to be removed. Highway 70 east of the West Branch of the Feather River was closed.
Heavy rain caused sheet flow from the Camp Fire burn scar, which flooded Highway 99 near Neal Road.
Flooding was reported at Honey Run Road and Horse Run Lane in Chico, due to local ponding of water and runoff from the Camp Fire burn scar.
A vehicle was reported stuck in flood waters up to mirrors in about 3.5 feet of water.
There were 1.03 inches of rain over 12 hours in East Quincy.
There was 1.49 inches of rain over 10 hours in Shingletown.
There was 12 inches of snow reported at Northstar Ski Resort. Holiday travel was impacted by long delays and chain controls.
There was 11 inches of snow reported at Alpine Meadows Ski Resort. Holiday travel was impacted by long delays and chain controls.
There was 10 inches of snow reported at Sugar Bowl Ski Resort. Holiday travel was impacted by long delays and chain controls.
Downtown Sacramento set a daily record for rainfall, 1.17 inches of rain, breaking the old record of 0.95 inches set in 2002.
Red Bluff set a daily record for rainfall, 1.77 inches of rain, breaking the old record of 1.25 inches set in 1962.

Caltrans reported 46 inches of snow at Castle Peak, 22 inches at Kingvale. Pacific House received 3.0 inches of snow, Kyburz 2.25 inches, Camino 7 inches. This brought chain controls and delays on mountain highways.

There were chain controls in place on Interstate 80, Highway 50, State Route 4 (SR-4) in Calaveras County and Alpine County, SR-88 in Amador and Alpine counties and SR-108 in Tuolumne County. Snow amounts reported were 8 inches at Dodge Ridge, 6 inches at Castle Peak, 5 inches at Donner Ski Ranch, and 4 inches at Sugar Bowl.
The California Highway Patrol reported heavy rain caused flooding on Highway 16 in Woodland.
A video from Gridley, CA showed lighting striking a power pole.
California Highway Patrol reported heavy rain caused flooding of Highway 99 in Galt.
California Highway Patrol reported heavy rain caused flooding of the southbound lane of Interstate 5 in downtown Sacramento.
There was a public report of a possible funnel cloud near southwest Oroville. No touch down was observed.
A spotter reported a 12 hour rainfall total of 0.82.
A gust of 69 mph was measured 3 miles east southeast of Anderson.

Heavy snow was reported across the northern Sierra: 29 Alpine Ski Resort, 19 at Kirkwood Ski Resort, 14  at Sierra at Tahoe, 15 at Sugar Bowl. This caused travel delays and chain controls on mountain highways such as I80 and Highway 50.
A wind gust to 60 mph was measured at McClellan Airfield. Numerous trees were reported down in the area.
County Road 30 near Yolo Airport was closed due to flooding. Report from the CHP.
Heavy rains led to intense flooding in Red Bluff leading to 30 homes being evacuated on Aloha Street. Several homes did flood and evacuation orders were lifted at 1100 am.
Cottonwood Road closed between Highway 99 and Table Mountain Blvd. due to flooding.
River Road closed between Chico River Road and West Sacramento Ave. because of flooding.
Hamilton Nord Cana Hwy. closed from Bennet Rd. to Cana Hwy. because of flooding.
A member of the public observed flooded roads in Palermo, CA. Video footage showed water flowing over the road with water making it up to the businesses on either side.
Stockton Blvd was impassable due to flooding.
Between 5 and 6 am a vide of someone driving across flooded roads was posted on social media.
Highway 16 had east and west bound lanes flooded at County Road 89 near Guys Corner. A vehicle was submerged in flood waters. Flooding was first reported at 11 am.
Roadway flooding reported at SR16 pff ramp at I505S in Madison, with full closure for north and south bound I505.
Highway 162 closed between 1st St. and County Rd. 9 in Willows because of storm related flooding.
Local media shared a video of law enforcement rescuing a stranded motorist in Sloughhouse near Kiefer Blvd and Jackson Rd. Road was completely flooded.
There was a 12 hour total of 2.1 of rain. Slush from earlier snow was blocking street drains with ponding water observed.
Trees were damaged near the intersection of Highway 16 and Highway 49.
Two funnel clouds were observed northeast of Bellotta, Twitter Report.

NWS Sacramento received a message via twitter about damage received from a line of showers moving through Lake county the evening of January 16th, 2019.  A trailer was lifted, a metal awning was ripped off, an outdoor range was pushed over, and many large branches were broken off.

Rock and Debris flow over the Butte County Camp fire due to heavy rain at the Crests Powerhouse. Also CalTrans had some nearby debris issues that they have addressed with maintenance but do not know the extent. Rock slides are common in this particular slide area was a result of heavy rain on the Camp Fire.

On April 12, the high temperature reached 89 degrees at Stockton Airport.  This tied the daily high temperature record, which was last reached in 1977.||On April 12, the high temperature reached 92 degrees at Modesto.  This broke the previous daily high temperature record of 91 degrees set in 1962.||On April 13, the high temperature reached 93 degrees at Stockton Airport.  This broke the previous daily high temperature record of 91 degrees set in 1962.
The high temperature reached 87 degrees at Sacramento Executive Airport.  This tied the daily high temperature record, which was last reached in 1990.

On February 2, 2019 there was a brief tornado touchdown at the Sacramento River National Wildlife Refuge north of Colusa. A weather spotter took a video of the touchdown, which occurred in a wetlands area. No damage was reported.

National Weather Service meteorologists confirmed an EF0 tornado touched down at approximately 5:50 pm pst on Saturday, February 2nd, just south of Yuba City, CA. This tornado touch down was very brief as it tracked to the north northwest. Radar data and the damage pattern were used to confirm the touchdown. Several trees were knocked down and there was minor roof damage to a home. Leaves and branches were completely stripped off one side of a tree.
Half dollar hail reported north of Colusa.
A trained spotter reported a well defined wall cloud with a funnel cloud north of Colusa.
Tuolumne County Sheriffs Office reports there are road closures along Red Hills Road in Chinese Camp, Sims Road in Jamestown, and Bell Mooney Road in Jamestown.
Wind caused tree and fence damage near Carlson Road and Hutchinson Road in Yuba City.
A social media user reported flooding on Highway 99, north of Chico. Cars were seen driving through water.
Caltrans District 3 reported that flooding has closed Highway 162 between 1st Street and County Rd P east of Willows in Glenn County.
Caltrans reported a flooded roadway in northern Willows.

Accumulating snow fell, causing slippery mountain roads. A COOP observer in Chester reported 5 inches of snowfall in 24 hours and a storm total of 15 inches (elevation 4530 feet). Quincy reported a storm total of 10.

Accumulating heavy, wet snow fell into the Motherlode foothills, causing major winter weather impacts. The biggest impacts were south of Highway 50. A CoCoRaHS observer at Tuolumne City reporting 7 inches of snow, unusual for the area. The heavy snow brought down many hundreds of trees & limbs, blocking roads at times and bringing down numerous power lines. Nearly 40,000 PG&E customers were reported without power in Tuolumne and Calaveras counties. Some power outages lasted several days before crews could reach and repair the lines. More than 40 schools closed down in Tuolumne and Calaveras counties, as well as most county offices and many businesses. Even snow plows got stuck on Highway 49 due to the heavy snow. Snow reached down to to as low as 750 feet elevation briefly. A CoCoRaHS observer 2.5 miles E of Shingletown had 7 of snow, a spotter reported 6.25 inches of snow in Placerville (elevation 2250 feet), and the Grass Valley COOP reported 2.4.

Very heavy snow fell, bringing whiteout conditions and extremely slippery conditions. I-80 was shut down for 24 hours, from 9 am on Monday the 4th to 9 am on Tuesday the 5th, causing major travel and commerce disruptions.||Here are some of the higher reported storm totals: 92 at Castle Peak (Donner Pass), 92 at Kirkwood Ski Resort, 84 at Squaw Valley Ski Resort, 83 at Bear Valley Ski Resort, and 80 at Sugar Bowl Ski Resort.
Accumulating snow fell, causing slippery mountain roads. A spotter reported 8 inches of snow in Fall River Mills (elevation 3300 feet).

Accumulating snow fell into the northeast foothills, with a CoCoRaHS observer 2.5 miles east of Shingletown reporting 6.4 inches of new snow in 24 hours. This caused travel significant delays on area roads.

Heavy snow caused chain controls, travel restrictions and closures on mountain highways. I80 was closed for about an hour eastbound and westbound between Colfax and the Nevada state line. ||Caltrans reported 60 of snow over 24 hours at Castle Peak (Donner Pass) with a storm total of 68 of snow over 48 hours. Squaw Valley Ski Resort had 46 over 24 hours. Kingvale had 45 over 48 hours, 44 over 72 hours for CoCoRaHS 1.5 SSW Soda Springs.  Other 24 hour reports: Alpine Meadows Ski Resort had 38, Sierra at Tahoe 37, Boreal 36, Kirkwood 31, Bear Valley 30, Pacific House 17.

Heavy snow caused travel delays on foothill highways and some reported downed trees and local power outages. A trained spotter in Placerville at elevation 2,180 ft reported 3 inches of snow, 2 inches of snow at Jamestown (in 24 hours). Social media had a report of 7 inches at in 24 hours in Tuolumne at an elevation of 2800 ft and a trace of snow in Volcano at elevation 2800 ft. A downed tree caused some power outages in Sonora.
Heavy snow caused travel delays on mountain highways. The Chester COOP had a storm total of 9 inches of new snow, the Quincy COOP observer reported a storm total of 7 inches.

Snow caused travel delays on foothill highways.  The COOP observer at Montgomery Creek reported a storm total of 8 inches of new snow. CoCoRaHS observers at Shingletown 5.3 ENE had a total of 5 inches, Shingletown 2.5 E had 6.4 inches.
A trained spotter at Hobergs (3,250 ft elevation) reported a snow total of 5 inches of snow. This caused travel delays in the area.
California Highway reported county roads closed due to flooding.
California Highway Patrol reported road flooding with #1 lane blocked on highway 160 s and del paso boulevard on ramp.
California Highway Patrol reported country roads closed due to flooding.
On Twitter Cal Fire Butte unit/Butte County Fire Department reported that a couple miles away at West Sacramento Avenue and River Road, water was flowing freely across the road.
California Highway Patrol reported slight flooding over Willow Creek Bridge on SB Interstate 5 north of Willows.
Stockton police reported road flooding at Claremont Avenue and Sousa Street, Stockton and has closed both directions of the road.
On twitter the city of Vacaville relayed a flooding report from the Vacaville PD to avoid Vanden Road between Canon Road and Peabody Road until further notice, due to flooding.

The media reported that they received information from the California Highway Patrol that a vehicle was swept into Scotts Creek as they were trying to cross a flooded roadway. 3 people were rescued from the car.
On twitter the public information officer from Metro fire of Sacramento posted about a swift water rescue that occurred on Feb 13 at 4:44 pm. on Kiefer Blvd north of Jackson Rd.
Caltrans and law enforcement started receiving reports of washed out roads and flooding around 2:30 am. A full closure of Hwy 20 is in effect as of 1:40pm.

Caltrans reported that both lanes of the road were flooded. At 10:46am Caltrans reported that the flooding was caused by debris build up.
Butte County Sheriff evacuated the area of Nord Cana Highway and Wilson Landing Road south of Rock Creek after a levee breached and the creek flooded.

Caltrans reported flooding on pool station road at 9am with the road closing at 9:30am. at 12:05 pm new reports came in that pool station bridge near riata is washed away and that warning signs were put up. Multiple vehicles were still trying to get through.
Over 2-3 hours 1.5 to 2.5 inches of rain fell. A mudslide was reported at this particular location with the road being closed from Woodhouse Mine to West Point.
Caltrans reported that the river was running across the roadway way and that highway 4 needed to be closed. At 11:53 am Caltrans sent a notification that Highway 49 was reopened.

Caltrans is reporting that the roadway is completely flooded.
Local media reporting flood waters running over Pool Station Road caused road on bridge to crack.

Caltrans reported that roadway was flooded.
In Yolo and Colusa Counties, Hwy 16 had eastbound lanes closed at Hwy 20 and westbound lanes closed at Rumsey Canyon due to rock slides. The closest 24 hour rain report had 2.06 inches of rain.
Caltrans at Route 53 south, there is a full closure of Hwy 20 due to flooding.

The media reported that late in the evening on February 13, 2018 two people had been rescued from the roof of a car at Cox Lane and Lone Tree Road near Palermo. This information came from the public information officer for Cal Fire-Butte County.

Via a Facebook live with CBS13 and the Williams Fire Department Chief reported that 6 swift water rescues have occurred today. One was on going at the time of report which included a child and an adult. The fire chief estimated that there was 3-6 feet of flowing water over the roads. Both I-5 and old Highway 99 were closed for flooding.

The county reported there were numerous reports of blocked roads due to mudslides and 25 reports of flooded roads across Calaveras County. A line of storms remained stationary over this area with 1.0 inch of rain being reported in an hour which caused these conditions.
Via Twitter, Placer County reported that Dowd Road at Wise Road near Lincoln was closed due to flooding.

The media reported that part of New Hope Marina Trailer Park flooded. Local law enforcement arrived to help residents evacuate the area. The manager of the trailer part said that most residents evacuated or moved trailers on their own.

Via twitter Cal Fire Butte County Fire Department reported that firefighters were searching in the area of Lower Honcut road and Hwy 70. They located a truck and horse trailer under water that was swept 150 feet off the roadway. Believed driver was out of the vehicle.
Swift water team and Butte County Search and Rescue responded to Ord Ferry Road after the driver of a semi-trailer truck attempted to cross a flooded road.

Heavy snow fell over portions of the northern Sacramento Valley shutting down Interstate 5 south of the Oregon border through Redding and knocking out power to thousands of customers. Thousands of trees were reported down by county officials.||Schools closed, Shasta County Superior Court shut down and flights were canceled at Redding Airport. Some 83,600 customers lost power as trees and their branches heavy with snow fell onto power lines. The majority of those who lost power were in Shasta County. The California Highway Patrol reported dozens of spinouts, fallen trees blocking roads and vehicles in ditches throughout Shasta County.||A trained spotter reported that 13.5 inches of snow had accumulated 1/2 a mile from downtown Redding.  Another spotter sent a report through Facebook estimating that 12 inches of snow had accumulated on the ground 3 WSW Redding.

Heavy snow and whiteout conditions caused I80 to be closed for February 15th for the morning through 6 pm. Avalanche control and a fallen tree also kept closed Highway 50 much of the day. These closures caused major impacts to travel and interstate commerce.||Castle Peak had a storm total of 45 inches of new snow. Squaw Valley Ski Resort at 8,000 feet reported 30 inches of new snow over 24 hours. At 6200 feet 20 inches was reported over 24 hours. Soda Springs had a storm total of 40 inches.

Caltrans reported 40 inches of snow at Donner Pass, (elevation 7100 feet) over 24 hours, 44 inches storm total, Kingvale (elevation 6200 feet) 7 inches over 24 hours, 26 inches storm total. Cabbage Patch along Highway 4 had 10 inches of snow. A CoCoRaHS observer reported 30 inches at Soda Springs. ||Strong winds occurred over the Sierra crest with this storm, gusting to 122 mph at Ward Mt. at Alpine Ski Resort (8483 feet), 110 mph at Sierra Crest in Squaw Valley Ski Resort (8700 feet) on the 25th. Winds were also gusty below the crest, such as 62 mph at Emigrant Gap (5337 feet). These winds when combined with heavy snow brought periods of whiteout conditions, bringing hazardous driving conditions.

Mt. Shasta Ski Resort reported a storm total of 36 inches of snow. This caused chain controls and travel delays on mountain roads.||Gusty winds occurred, up to 49 mph at Colby Mountain and 42 mph at Humbug Summit, on the 25th. This along with heavy snow brought poor visibility at times.
Heavy rain in Lake County over 2 inches 24hr elevation 3200 feet.
Highway 49 closed at Newtown Rd to Tyler-Foote due to a rock slide, 1 to 2 inches of rain in the last 24 hours.
Heavy rain, 3.48 inches in 12 hours, 5.12 inches in 24 hours.

Oroville Dam Blvd E roadway was flooded and completely blocked.
Roadway flooding reported by CHP at 1619 Poole Blvd, Yuba City.

E I80 BY Longview Dr. flooded.

Auburn Folsom Rd at Cavitt Atallman Rd. Roadway flooded and water had risen to edge of roadway.

Evacuation of all residences on Taffee Ave, Reavis Ave and Chico Ave due to flooding in area from Little Chico Creek.
Evacuations of Safari Mobile Home Park due to floodwaters backing up from the Anderson-Cottonwood Canal and Olney Creek.
There were 6 inches of water in lane number 1 of Capitol City Freeway.

Downed tree blocked right NB lane of Highway 49. A gust to 50 mph was measured at Pike County Lookout.

A funnel cloud and possible rotating wall cloud were reported by two spotters over the Colusa National Wildlife Refuge area. Also, hail as large as one half inch in diameter accumulated to 2 inches deep on Highway 45 between Grimes and Sycamore.

Roadway flooding reported by the CHP at Cow Creek Ranch Road and Whitmore Road, including a small mudslide on the westbound Lane.

A 56 year old man was found dead after three rafters fell into the North Fork of the American River near Colfax on the evening of Saturday, May 4th, according to Cal Fire and the Placer County Sheriff���s Office. He was found Sunday by park rangers and recovered by Placer County sheriff���s dive teams near Lake Clementine, according to a news release by the sheriff���s office. The other 2 men were rescued. There were numerous reports of roadway flooding in Stockton due to heavy rain and large amounts of small accumulating hail on May 19th. Law enforcement reported March Lane and Quail Lakes being shut down along with Hammer Lane between Lorraine Ave and Girardi Way due to flooding.

A COCORAHS observer reported 12 inches of snow in 24 hours at elevation 6768 on the morning of May 19th.

A CoCoRaHS observer in Soda Springs reported 4 inches of snowfall in 24 hours at elevation 6,768 feet. Alpine Meadows Ski Resort reported 5 inches of snowfall at elevation 8,000 feet. Minor travel delays occurred on Interstate 80.
There was 1 1/2 feet of water flooding the west bound lane of I80.
Roadway flooding on State Route 124 on Placer County side of border just east of Bear River.
Flooding of entire west bound off-ramp of I80 in Colfax.

There were numerous reports of large hail across the Redding area, including a photo of hail from the family of an NWS employee showing oblong hail as large as 3 inches in diameter. Hail this size is rare in California and is near record size. Many cars were dented or had back windows or windshields broken. A preliminary estimate of damage to hail is based on a KRCR story of up to 3000 cars damaged and a national average of $2500 for damage repairs (Auto Trends).  This works out to rough estimated of around $7.5 million for auto damage alone. Some building damage was also reported, including the Northern California Geographic Area Coordination Center, which suffered damage to a new roof.

Hail caused damage to fruit in the Gold Hill area, near Placerville. Farmers in the area generally had 50% crop damage, with a few losing 90% of their crop. El Dorado County officials reported a damage estimate of $286,000.
Clearlake Rd. had flooding reported.

Social media reported local street flooding.
CHP reported road flooding at Larkin Rd.
A funnel cloud was reported in southwest Redding. No touchdown or damage was reported.
Quarter size hail was reported near Enterprise High School in Redding.
On Twitter, a user reported ping pong ball sized hail near Hartnell Ave and Victor Ave in Redding, CA.
At Redding Airport, a 58 MPH wind gust was reported.
A PGE weather station on Concow Road at an elevation of 2785 feet reported a 58 MPH wind gust. Prior to this observation the station reported gusts between 35-44 MPH.
A trained spotter located in Cobb reported 1.5 inches of snow at elevation 4700 feet on May 19th.
On May 19th, at an elevation of 4400 feet, a CoCoRaHS observer reported 2 inches of snow.

On June 8, conditions were favorable for wildfire growth as relative humidity values fell into the teens and northerly winds gusted up to 25-45 mph. Prior to the start of this event, the local utility company decided to de-energize power lines per CA Public Utility Commissions (CPUC) Public Safety Power Shutoff (PSPS) guidelines. Eventually, a fire did start at 1350PST in Yolo County, which became known as the Sand Fire. There were 2512 acres of land burned over a period of 8 days, along with 7 structures destroyed. The fire also led to road closures from Highway 16 to Highway 20 to the town Brooks in addition to the evacuation of residents living along County Road 41.

On the evening of June 18th a woman reported that her boyfriend was swept away by fast-moving water in the West Branch of the Feather River, near the end of Dean Road in Paradise, CA. The next day authorities were able to recover the victim.

On June 19th, a group of friends had been swimming in the Cosumnes River at Highway 49, near the Amador-El Dorado County line. Around 1130PST, a call was made to local authorities that a teenage boy was pulled under by rapids and disappeared. Two hours later, rescue teams were able to recover the victim.

On June 23, Nevada County Sheriff's Office received a call that a swimmer went into the water of the Emerald Pools Recreation Area, was overtaken by the current, and that the group of friends lost sight of him. A multi-agency search and rescue was started that afternoon, but the victim was not recovered until the following day. The Sheriff's office noted that the water temperature was about 40 degrees Fahrenheit for this event.

The Rock Fire started Tuesday night June 25th, 4 miles Del Puerto Canyon Rd, which is west of Patterson. It grew to 2422 acres over 24 hours and according to a CalFire via a media interview, the fire was burning near several Native American archaeological sites belonging to the Yokuts. Crews took extra precautions not to disturb the soil of these sites and at the time of the media report, it was unknown if the fire had done any damage. Additionally, it was also noted in a media interview that some acres of ranch land were burned but no buildings or structures were.
A debris fire in Cold Springs in Tuolumne County got out of control in windy conditions, spreading to 20 acres and destroying one home.

On the evening on July 13, around 1700 PST, a young girl fell into the South Yuba River where it intersects with Highway 49. The father of the child jumped in after her and then went missing around 1740 PST. State park officials were able to rescue the daughter; however, they were not able to find the father as he was swept away down stream. Ultimately his body was recovered on July 21, 2019 at 1145 PST about a half mile downstream from the Highway 49 bridge. The news article noted that the Sheriff's office said that the South Yuba River was flowing at four to five times normal because of all the snow melt.

On the evening of July 24th at 1700 PST three people were swimming in the Feather River Canyon when suddenly they started to be carried away by the current. Two of the swimmers escaped; however, the third person, a 9 year old child, did not. His body was located around 2000 PST under the Tobin Bridge.

On July 17, 2019 the Plumas County Sheriff's Office posted on their Facebook page about a cold water death that occurred near the Rock Creek Bridge on Highway 70 in the Feather River Canyon. The Sheriff's Office received the call at 1434PST that a victim had fallen into the water while hiking and at the time of call they were still submerged underwater. Efforts were made by the victim���s husband to pull her out of the rapids but the current was too strong. The victim's body was recovered at 1744PST.

On August 15th a wildfire was reported in the community of Millville in Shasta County. This fire burned a 156 acres over a period of two days during a brief heatwave over northern California. On Calfire's web page for the Cottage Fire, it notes that one fire fighter was injured due to heat related illness. An Excessive Heat Warning was in place from 1100 August 14 to 2100 August 16.

On Friday, August 9, roughly 7 miles to the northwest of Red Bluff, a strong thunderstorm produced 1 inch hail stones that fell for 5 to 10 minutes. The public reported that they noticed some minor damage to trees and plants in the area.
A severe thunderstorm produced up to 1.5 inch diameter hail stones on the north side of Black Butte Lake near the Buck Horn Campground. The time stamp for this report was estimated by radar.

CalFire reported that a wildfire occurred on the morning of August 22 and lasted through the evening of August 26. This fire was named the Mountain Fire and burned 600 acres of land. It damaged 5 residential buildings and 2 additional structures in addition to destroying 7 residential buildings and 7 other structures.  A local news paper also reported that about 14 wooden power poles were damaged and that the local power company worked actively to replace them. CalFire also noted that there were 3 cases of minor injuries, and that all the victims were treated and released. There were numerous evacuations, around 3,885 residents, and road closures within the area which were all lifted on the by the evening of August 24.

Multiple news outlets reported that a 41 year old man had either fallen or jumped off a boat on the evening of September 2. A music event was on going at this time, but given that the water was dark and murky, the man was unable to be retrieved. Local law enforcement was able to recover the man's body about 45 minutes after he fell in and tried to resuscitate him, but failed. The corner ruled the man's death a drowning.

events.cz_name: MOUNTAINS SOUTHWEST SHASTA COUNTY TO NORTHERN LAKE COUNTY
events.event_narrative: On September 5 thunderstorms developed over interior northern California sparking several wildfires within the region. This particular fire was named the South Fire and it grew up to 5,332 acres, with the majority of the fire growth occurring between September 5-21. Terrain is steep and rugged out there, which made containment difficult and called for road closures at times. The last major update that the Shasta-Trinity National Forest Service put out was on September 21, 2019; however, on November 27, 2019 at 10AM PST, they reported the fire was officially 100% contained and controlled.

events.cz_name: MOUNTAINS SOUTHWEST SHASTA COUNTY TO NORTHERN LAKE COUNTY
events.event_narrative: On September 5 thunderstorms developed over interior northern California sparking several wildfires within the region. This particular fire was named the Red Bank Fire and it grew up to 8,838 acres. This fire damaged or destroyed 2 structures and caused road closures and mandatory evacuations. Evacuations were lifted by the evening of September 8.

On September 7, a fire broke out in Butte County and burned 496 acres of land, destroying 2 buildings one residential and outbuilding. The fire grew fast enough to warrant mandatory evacuations and road closures, which were all eventually lifted by the evening of September 9th. The fire was declared contained on September 13, 2019 at 6PM PST.
The California Highway Patrol reported that there was flooding on the bridge between Gyle and Finnel roads and that vehicles were sliding around because of it.
A member of the public saw and photographed a small funnel cloud near Loma Rica. No contact with the ground was observed.
The Squaw Alpine Ski Resort tweeted a picture of snow covering the ground on their high Camp Slope. Estimated snow depth from picture would be 1 to 2 inches.
A walnut tree was snapped 3 miles north of Marysville on highway 70. Time stamp of wind gust damage is estimated based on radar.

The media shared a wind damage report from the public which included images and videos. A hay barn and horse stable had pole and roof damage that can clearly be seen in the footage. The RAWS weather station at OpenShaw, which is close to the damage site, reported a 50 mph wind gust.

Minor debris and rock slides blocked highway 70 from Jarbo Gap to Greenville Way (Junction of state route 70 and state route 89). Road culverts were blocked with debris requiring lane closures. The debris flow is associated with the Camp Fire burn area.
The public reported mud and rocks in the roadway on highway 49 between Nevada City on the South Yuba River. Time is estimated by radar.

The local news paper reported that multiple members of the public were sending in reports of localized street flooding in Nevada City. This particular point does not necessarily reflect the exact location of flooding and the time of this report is based on  radar and observations.
A spotter SO47, located on highway 113 north of Davis, reported one inch hail stones.
A tornado was reported by a University of California Davis atmospheric science student. The student was reported to be east of highway 101a and highway 29 around 5:41 pm pst and filmed the tornado.
A member of the public reported a funnel cloud about 2 miles east of El Macero Country Club.

A member of the public called to inform us about hail damage to their pistachio crop. They estimated that the hail stone sizes were generally around 0.75-1.0 inch stones but that they also varied greatly in size as it fell. After the hail ended they went to check on their pistachio crop and found out that they lost all of it. These trees were about 30 years old and sustained damaged.

At the Lassen National Park Visitor Center, which is at an elevation of 6700 feet, 6 to 8 inches of snow fell overnight. the park ranger noted that at about 7000 feet there were higher amounts but it was still snowing pretty heavily up there at the time of report.They also noted that prior to last night, each day they may have received a trace amount of snow.

The mesonet stations for Jarbo Gap and Concow Road observed strong non-thunderstorm related wind gusts that ranged from 30-51 mph. Once the wind event was completed, the local power utility company surveyed the area for damage and found a downed tree near some power lines and an ensnared branch in the power lines. These items were removed the company stated that no damage was done to their equipment.

On October 10 a prescribed burn, which was started on September 30, was declared a wild fire incident. Extreme fire weather conditions were forecast which led to the growth of the prescribed burn. In total 3435 acres were burned across the month of October. The Forest Service noted that 7 injuries or illnesses happened on this fire.

Redding Airport a non-thunderstorm related wind gust up to 66 mph. A debris fire in the town of Rescue in El Dorado County spread out of control over 15 acres. Fifty homes were threatened, with one home destroyed and one resident of that home suffering burn injuries.

A cool airmass along with light winds allowed temperatures to drop to 32 degrees at the Stockton Airport. This broke the daily low temperature record of 35 degrees set in 1967. Frost damage to wine grapes was reported, along with walnuts and some orchard fruits.

A cool airmass along with light winds allowed morning temperatures at the Redding Airport to reach 31 degrees, setting a new daily low temperature record. This broke the old record of 35 degrees set at the airport in 1996, and at the old city station in 1984. Frost damage to young walnuts was reported over portions of the northern Sacramento Valley.

A cool, dry airmass with light winds allowed temperatures to drop to 34 degrees at the Sacramento Exectuive Airport on April 20th, setting a new daily low temperature record. The old record was 36 degrees, set in 1967. Some frost damage to grapes was reported over portions of the southern Sacramento valley.

A cool airmass and light morning winds brought cold lows and frost to the area. Walnuts, peaches, prunes, and canning tomatoes were reported to have suffered frost damage in some areas, particularly in Butte and Sutter counties.

The Redding ASOS station reported a 45 mph wind gust. Gusty northerly winds were observed across the zone and caused damage. The timing for this event is based on the Redding ASOS report.

A giant rock wall will be constructed across a river in the Sacramento-San Joaquin River Delta to protect a vital freshwater estuary from saltwater as rivers become too low to push the brackish waters from the bay. The $30 million barrier will be built in the same place as it was in 2015 on the West False River to keep saltwater away from pumping stations. This will protect a water source for nearly 30 million Californians. Construction slated to begin by June 1 and be complete by July 1. The barrier will be removed before Nov. 30. Farmers north and south of the Sacramento-San Joaquin River Delta will receive no water from the Central Valley Project. The agency previously had forecast a 5% allocation. On May 10th, governor Gavin Newsom included all of zone 18 in the official drought emergency proclamation. The Delta cross channel gates were closed on May 20th.

High pressure ridging brought a heat wave to Northern California over the Memorial Day weekend holiday. Temperatures reached upwards of 20 to 25 degrees above climatology. Several new record daily high temperatures and one record monthly high temperature record were set in the area. At the peak of the heat wave on the 31st, Redding reached 109 breaking both the daily and monthly high temperature records. Red Bluff reached 108, setting a new daily high temperature record. Downtown Sacramento hit 106 tying the daily high temperature record. Sacramento Executive Airport reached 105 setting a new daily high temperature record. There were three cooling centers open in Sacramento County, one in Yolo County, one in Butte County and one in San Joaquin County.

The Salt Fire began on June 30, 2021, near Lakehead by Shasta Lake, in Shasta-Trinity National Forest in Shasta County. The fire was determined to be caused by a vehicle. For the month of June, the U.S. Drought Monitor did not make changes to Zone 13 which covers northwestern Shasta County. The majority of zone 13 was in exceptional drought (D4) with the remaining areas of Zone 13 in extreme drought (D3). They continue to mention that we will see drought impacts expand into the summer, including but not limited too: agriculture, water supplies, recreation, and ecosystems. They also noted concern for the wildfire season given the rapid spread and community impacts from the Salt Fire that started near Lakehead, CA. Drought preparedness is a top priority given back-to-back dry years. All of Zone 13 is in the official drought emergency proclamation. On June 15th, the Shasta County Board of Supervisors declared a countywide drought emergency and included a water conservation program.

They continue to mention that we will see drought impacts expand into the summer, including but not limited too: agriculture, water supplies, recreation, and ecosystems. They also noted concern for the wildfire season and that drought preparedness is key given back-to-back dry years. Some of the impacts the region saw included: reduced forage, decreased stock weights, selling of livestock, livestock stress, reduced grazing on public lands, reduced market price for cattle, and increased pricing for small grain and hay crops. The area also saw: decreased water allocation, hauling of water, increased groundwater use, land subsidence, low to dry rivers/ponds/springs, dry wells, and installation of new wells. All of zone 15 is in the official drought emergency proclamation. On June 15th, the Shasta County Board of Supervisors declared a countywide drought emergency and included a water conservation program.

A giant rock wall started constructed across a river in the Sacramento-San Joaquin River Delta on June 3rd to protect a vital freshwater estuary from saltwater as rivers became too low to push the brackish waters from the bay. The rock barrier was built in the same place as it was in 2015 on the West False River to keep saltwater away from pumping stations. This will protect a water source for nearly 30 million Californians. Construction completed on June 22nd. The barrier will be removed before Nov. 30. They continue to mention impacts to: agriculture, water supplies, recreation, and ecosystems. By November, it was reported that an estimated 2.6% of endangered juvenile winter-run Chinook salmon survived the season leading to concern about the future of the species. Drought conditions may continue to improve as we continue into the rainy season that started October 1st.
